<h1 id="brevo-api">Brevo API v3.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Brevo provide a RESTFul API that can be used with any languages. With this API, you will be able to :
  - Manage your campaigns and get the statistics
  - Manage your contacts
  - Send transactional Emails and SMS
  - and much more...

You can download our wrappers at https://github.com/orgs/brevo
**Possible responses**
  | Code | Message |
  | :-------------: | ------------- |
  | 200  | OK. Successful Request  |
  | 201  | OK. Successful Creation |
  | 202  | OK. Request accepted |
  | 204  | OK. Successful Update/Deletion  |
  | 400  | Error. Bad Request  |
  | 401  | Error. Authentication Needed  |
  | 402  | Error. Not enough credit, plan upgrade needed  |
  | 403  | Error. Permission denied  |
  | 404  | Error. Object does not exist |
  | 405  | Error. Method not allowed  |
  | 406  | Error. Not Acceptable  |
  | 422  | Error. Unprocessable Entity |

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.brevo.com/v3">https://api.brevo.com/v3</a>

Email: <a href="mailto:contact@brevo.com">Brevo Support</a> 
Web: <a href="https://account.brevo.com/support">Brevo Support</a> 
License: <a href="http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT">MIT</a>

# Authentication

* API Key (api-key)
    - Parameter Name: **api-key**, in: header. The API key should be passed in the request headers as `api-key` for authentication.

* API Key (partner-key)
    - Parameter Name: **partner-key**, in: header. The partner key should be passed in the request headers as `partner-key` along with `api-key` pair for successful authentication of partner (Optional).

<h1 id="brevo-api-account">Account</h1>

## Get account details

<a id="opIdgetAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/account \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /account`

Retrieves details of your Brevo account.

**Use this to:**
- Get account information (email, name, company, address)
- Check plan details (type, credits, expiration)
- Get relay information (for transactional emails)
- Check Marketing Automation status
- Access organization and user identifiers

**Key information returned:**
- Complete account details (organization ID, user ID, company information)
- Address and contact information
- Plan configurations and credit allocations across different verticals
- Marketing Automation settings and tracker key (when enabled)
- SMTP relay configuration for transactional emails
- Enterprise features availability status

**Important considerations:**
- Provides comprehensive account overview for billing and configuration management
- Essential for understanding current plan limitations and feature availability
- Marketing Automation key is only returned when Marketing Automation is enabled on the account
- Plan verticals show detailed breakdown across Marketing, Chat, and CRM categories (only returned when plan verticals are available)
- Relay configuration crucial for transactional email setup and deliverability
- Enterprise status determines access to advanced features and sub-account management

## Get user activity logs

<a id="opIdgetAccountActivity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/organization/activities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /organization/activities`

Retrieves user activity logs from your organization for security monitoring and audit compliance.

Use this to:
- Monitor user login activities and access patterns
- Track account modifications and configuration changes
- Generate security audit reports and compliance documentation
- Investigate suspicious activities and unauthorized access
- Monitor team member actions and account usage

Key information returned:
- Complete user activity details and timestamps
- User identification (email, IP address, browser)
- Action types and activity descriptions
- Security-relevant events and access logs
- Historical activity data for audit trails

Note: Requires Enterprise plan for access to organization activity logs.

<h3 id="get-user-activity-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startDate|query|string|false|Mandatory if endDate is used. Enter start date in UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD)<br>format to filter the activity in your account. Maximum time period that<br>can be selected is one month. Additionally, you can retrieve activity<br>logs from the past 12 months from the date of your search.|
|endDate|query|string|false|Mandatory if startDate is used. Enter end date in UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD)<br>format to filter the activity in your account. Maximum time period that<br>can be selected is one month.|
|email|query|string|false|Enter the user's email address to filter their activity in the account.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document in the page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "logs": [
    {
      "action": "login-success",
      "date": "2023-03-16T16:49:23+05:30",
      "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (iPad; U; CPU OS 3_2_1 like Mac OS X; en-us)",
      "user_email": "test@mycompany.com",
      "user_ip": "192.158.1.34"
    },
    {
      "action": "update-profile",
      "count": 2,
      "date": "2023-03-15T16:49:23+05:30",
      "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (iPad; U; CPU OS 3_2_1 like Mac OS X; en-us)",
      "user_email": "test@myexample.com",
      "user_ip": "192.158.1.38"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

<h1 id="brevo-api-master-account">Master account</h1>

## Create a new group of sub-accounts

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/corporate/group \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "groupName": "My group",
    "subAccountIds": [
      234322,
      325553,
      893432
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /corporate/group`

This endpoint allows to create a group of sub-accounts

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "groupName": "My group",
  "subAccountIds": [
    234322,
    325553,
    893432
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-group-of-sub-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» groupName|body|string|true|The name of the group of sub-accounts|
|» subAccountIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Pass the list of sub-account Ids to be included in the group|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "659xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx6ef9c8"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_parameter",
  "message": "Invalid request"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-group-of-sub-accounts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Group ID|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[errorModel](#schemaerrormodel)|

<h3 id="create-a-new-group-of-sub-accounts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api-key, partner-key
</aside>

## Delete sub-account from group

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/corporate/group/unlink/string/subAccounts \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "subAccountIds": [
      423432,
      234323,
      87678
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /corporate/group/unlink/{groupId}/subAccounts`

This endpoint allows you to remove a sub-organization from a group.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subAccountIds": [
    423432,
    234323,
    87678
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-sub-account-from-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Group id|
|body|body|object|true|List of sub-account ids|
|» subAccountIds|body|[integer(int64)]|true|List of sub-account ids|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_parameter",
  "message": "subAccountIds should be array of numeric ids only"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-sub-account-from-group-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|SubAccounts removed from the group|None|
|400|Bad Request|bad request|[errorModel](#schemaerrormodel)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api-key, partner-key
</aside>

## Delete a group

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/corporate/group/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /corporate/group/{id}`

This endpoint allows you to delete a group of sub-organizations. When a
group is deleted, the sub-organizations are no longer part of this group.
The users associated with the group are no longer associated with the group
once deleted.

## Generate SSO token to access admin account

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/corporate/ssoToken \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "vipin+ent-user@brevo.com"
  }'
```

`POST /corporate/ssoToken`

This endpoint generates an SSO token to authenticate and access the admin
account using the endpoint
https://account-app.brevo.com/account/login/corporate/sso/[token], where
[token] will be replaced by the actual token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "vipin+ent-user@brevo.com"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» email|body|string|true|User email of admin account|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "token": "5cadaxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx5a179f85a0"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_parameter",
  "message": "Invalid email address"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": "permission_denied",
  "message": "Access forbidden."
}
```

<h3 id="generate-sso-token-to-access-admin-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|

## Generate SSO token to access sub-account

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/corporate/subAccount/ssoToken \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "vipin+subaccount@brevo.com",
    "id": 3232323,
    "target": "contacts",
    "url": "https://app.brevo.com/senders/domain/list"
  }'
```

`POST /corporate/subAccount/ssoToken`

This endpoint generates an sso token to authenticate and access a
sub-account of the master using the account endpoint
https://account-app.brevo.com/account/login/sub-account/sso/[token], where
[token] will be replaced by the actual token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "vipin+subaccount@brevo.com",
  "id": 3232323,
  "target": "contacts",
  "url": "https://app.brevo.com/senders/domain/list"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-sso-token-to-access-sub-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» email|body|string|false|User email of sub-account organization|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|true|Id of the sub-account organization|
|» target|body|string|false|**Set target after login success** * **automation** - Redirect<br>to Automation after login * **email_campaign** - Redirect to<br>Email Campaign after login * **contacts** - Redirect to Contacts<br>after login * **landing_pages** - Redirect to Landing Pages<br>after login * **email_transactional** - Redirect to Email<br>Transactional after login * **senders** - Redirect to Senders<br>after login * **sms_campaign** - Redirect to Sms Campaign after<br>login * **sms_transactional** - Redirect to Sms Transactional<br>after login|
|» url|body|string|false|Set the full target URL after login success. The user will land<br>directly on this target URL after login|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» target|automation|
|» target|email_campaign|
|» target|contacts|
|» target|landing_pages|
|» target|email_transactional|
|» target|senders|
|» target|sms_campaign|
|» target|sms_transactional|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "token": "5cadaxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx5a179f85a0"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_parameter",
  "message": "Invalid sub-account id."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": "permission_denied",
  "message": "Access forbidden."
}
```

<h3 id="generate-sso-token-to-access-sub-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Session token|[getSsoToken](#schemagetssotoken)|
|400|Bad Request|bad request|[errorModel](#schemaerrormodel)|
|403|Forbidden|Current account is not a master account|[errorModel](#schemaerrormodel)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api-key, partner-key
</aside>

`DELETE /corporate/subAccount/{id}`

Permanently deletes a sub-account from the corporate master account. Once deleted, all data associated with the sub-account organization is removed and cannot be recovered, so ensure the sub-account is no longer needed before proceeding.

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/corporate/subAccount/0/plan \
```

`PUT /corporate/subAccount/{id}/plan`

This endpoint will update the sub-account plan. On the Corporate solution
new version v2, you can set an unlimited number of credits in your
sub-organization. Please pass the value “-1" to set the consumable in
unlimited mode.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "credits": {
    "email": 5000,
    "externalFeeds": 1,
    "sms": 2000,
    "whatsapp": 100,
    "wpSubscribers": -1
  },
  "features": {
    "inbox": 10,
    "landingPage": 20,
    "salesUsers": 6,
    "users": 15
  }
}
```

|» credits|body|object|false|Credit details to update|
|» » email|body|integer(int64)|false|Number of email credits \| Pass the value -1 for unlimited<br>emails in ENTv2 only|
|» » externalFeeds|body|number(int64)|false|Number of externalFeeds credits, possible values are 0 or 1<br>\|available in ENTv2 only|
|» » sms|body|number(float)|false|Number of SMS credits \| Pass the value -1 for unlimited SMS<br>in ENTv2 only|
|» » whatsapp|body|number(float)|false|Number of whatsapp credits \| Pass the value -1 for unlimited<br>whatsapp in ENTv2 only|
|» » wpSubscribers|body|integer(int64)|false|Number of Push credits, possible value is 0 and -1 \|<br>available in ENT-v2 only|
|» features|body|object|false|Features details to update|

|» » landingPage|body|integer(int64)|false|Number of landing pages|
|» » salesUsers|body|integer(int64)|false|Number of sales and service users \| only available in ENT-V2|
|» » users|body|integer(int64)|false|Number of multi-users|

|» » landingPage|body|integer(int64)|false|Number of landing pages|
|» » salesUsers|body|integer(int64)|false|Number of sales and service users \| only available in ENT-V2|

`POST /corporate/user/invitation/send`

`This endpoint allows you to invite a member to manage the Admin account
Features and their respective permissions are as below: - `my_plan`:
  - "all"
- `api`:
  - "none"
- `user_management`:
  - "all"
- `app_management` | Not available in ENTv2:
  - "all"
- `sub_organization_groups`
  - "create"
  - "edit_delete"
- `create_sub_organizations`
  - "all"
- `manage_sub_organizations`
  - "all"
- `analytics`
  - "download_data"
  - "create_alerts"
  - "my_looks"
  - "explore_create"
- `security`
  - "all"
**Note**: - If `all_features_access: false` then only privileges are
required otherwise if `true` then it's assumed that all permissions will be
there for the invited admin user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "all_features_access": true,
  "email": "inviteuser@example.com",
  "groupIds": [
    "2baxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxcaa",
    "65axxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxc5a"
  ],
  "privileges": [
    [
      {
        "feature": "my_plan",
        "permissions": [
          "all"
        ]
      },
      {
        "feature": "api",
        "permissions": [
          "none"
        ]
      },
      {
        "feature": "user_management",
        "permissions": [
          "all"
        ]
      },
      {
        "feature": "app_management",
        "permissions": [
          "all"
        ]
      },
      {
        "feature": "sub_organization_groups",
        "permissions": [
          "create",
          "edit_delete"
        ]
      },
      {
        "feature": "create_sub_organizations",
        "permissions": [
          "all"
        ]
      },
      {
        "feature": "manage_sub_organizations",
        "permissions": [
          "all"
        ]
      },
      {
        "feature": "analytics",
        "permissions": [
          "download_data",
          "create_alerts",
          "my_looks",
          "explore_create"
        ]
      },
      {
        "feature": "security",
        "permissions": [
          "all"
        ]
      }
    ]
  ]
}
```

## Get the list of all your users

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/organization/invited/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /organization/invited/users`

Retrieves the list of all users associated with your organization, including both active and pending invited users. Each user entry includes their email address, owner status, current invitation status, and feature access levels for marketing, CRM, and conversations.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "email": "owner@company.com",
      "feature_access": {
        "conversations": "owner",
        "crm": "owner",
        "marketing": "owner"
      },
      "is_owner": true,
      "status": "active"
    },
    {
      "email": "pendingInvitedUser@company.com",
      "feature_access": {
        "conversations": "none",
        "crm": "full",
        "marketing": "custom"
      },
      "is_owner": false,
      "status": "pending"
    },
    {
      "email": "connectedInvitedUser@company.com",
      "feature_access": {
        "conversations": "full",
        "crm": "none",
        "marketing": "none"
      },
      "is_owner": false,
      "status": "active"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "code": "method_not_allowed",

}
```

## Revoke user permission

<a id="opIdputRevokeUserPermission"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/organization/user/invitation/revoke/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`PUT /organization/user/invitation/revoke/{email}`

Revokes all permissions for an invited user in the organization, effectively removing their access to the platform. If the user''s plan change generated credit notes, they are returned in the response for billing reconciliation.

<h3 id="revoke-user-permission-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email|path|string|true|Email of the invited user.|

```json
  "status": "OK"
}
```

## Send invitation to user

<a id="opIdinviteuser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/organization/user/invitation/send \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "all_features_access": true,
    "email": "inviteuser@example.com",
    "privileges": [
      [
        {
          "feature": "email_campaigns",
          "permissions": [
            "create_edit_delete",
            "send_schedule_suspend"
          ]
        },
        {
          "feature": "sms_campaigns",
          "permissions": [
            "create_edit_delete",
            "send_schedule_suspend"
          ]
        }
      ]
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /organization/user/invitation/send`

`Feature` - A Feature represents a specific functionality like Email
campaign, Deals, Calls, Automations, etc. on Brevo. While inviting a user,
determine which feature you want to manage access to. You must specify the
feature accurately to avoid errors. `Permission` - A Permission defines the
level of access or control a user has over a specific feature. While
inviting user, decide on the permission level required for the selected
feature. Make sure the chosen permission is related to the selected feature.
Features and their respective permissions are as below: - `email_campaigns`:
  - "create_edit_delete"
  - "send_schedule_suspend"
- `sms_campaigns`:
  - "create_edit_delete"
  - "send_schedule_suspend"
- `contacts`:
  - "view"
  - "create_edit_delete"
  - "import"
  - "export"
  - "list_and_attributes"
  - "forms"
- `templates`:
  - "create_edit_delete"
  - "activate_deactivate"
- `workflows`:
  - "create_edit_delete"
  - "activate_deactivate_pause"
  - "settings"
- `landing_pages`:
  - "all"
- `transactional_emails`:
  - "settings"
  - "logs"
- `smtp_api`:
  - "smtp"
  - "api_keys"
  - "authorized_ips"
- `user_management`:
  - "all"
- `sales_platform`:
  - "create_edit_deals"
  - "delete_deals"
  - "manage_others_deals_tasks"
  - "reports"
  - "settings"
- `phone`:
  - "all"
- `conversations`:
  - "access"
  - "assign"
  - "configure"
- `senders_domains_dedicated_ips`:
  - "senders_management"
  - "domains_management"
  - "dedicated_ips_management"
- `push_notifications`:
  - "view"
  - "create_edit_delete"
  - "send"
  - "settings"
- `companies`:
  - "manage_owned_companies"
  - "manage_other_companies"
  - "settings"
**Note**: - If `all_features_access: false` then only privileges are
required otherwise if `true` then it's assumed that all permissions will be
there for the invited user. - The availability of feature and its permission
depends on your current plan. Please select the features and permissions
accordingly.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "all_features_access": true,
  "email": "inviteuser@example.com",
  "privileges": [
    [
      {
        "feature": "email_campaigns",
        "permissions": [
          "create_edit_delete",
          "send_schedule_suspend"
        ]
      },
      {
        "feature": "sms_campaigns",
        "permissions": [
          "create_edit_delete",
          "send_schedule_suspend"
        ]
      }
    ]
  ]
}
```

## Resend / Cancel invitation

<a id="opIdputresendcancelinvitation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/organization/user/invitation/resend/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`PUT /organization/user/invitation/{action}/{email}`

Resends or cancels a pending invitation for a user in the organization, depending on the action path parameter. Use `resend` to send a new invitation email to the user, or `cancel` to revoke the pending invitation entirely and remove the user''s pending access.

|action|path|string|true|action|
|email|path|string|true|Email of the invited user.|

|action|cancel|

## Check user permission

<a id="opIdgetUserPermission"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/organization/user/string/permissions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /organization/user/{email}/permissions`

Retrieves the granular feature-level permissions assigned to a specific user in the organization, identified by their email address. The response includes the user''s current status (active or pending) and a detailed list of privileges specifying which features and permission levels are granted.

<h1 id="brevo-api-process">Process</h1>

## Get background processes

<a id="opIdgetProcesses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/processes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /processes`

Retrieves a list of background processes from your Brevo account with filtering and pagination.

**Use this to:**
- Monitor background process activity and status
- Track long-running operations and tasks
- Find process IDs for detailed status checking
- Review process history and performance
- Identify failed or stuck processes for troubleshooting

**Key information returned:**
- Process details (ID, name, status)
- Export download URLs for completed export processes
- Import details with CSV report URLs for completed import processes
- Total count of processes for pagination

**Important considerations:**
- Background processes handle long-running operations like imports and exports
- Process status indicates current state (queued, processing, completed)
- Export processes provide download URLs when completed
- Import processes provide CSV report URLs with details about problematic records
- Use pagination for accounts with many historical processes
- Sort options available for creation order (ascending or descending)
- Default limit is 10 results per page, maximum is 50


<h3 id="get-background-processes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number limitation for the result returned|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Beginning point in the list to retrieve from.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation.<br>Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 198,
  "processes": [
    {
      "id": 217,
      "name": "IMPORTUSER",
      "status": "completed",
      "info": {
        "import": {
          "invalid_emails": null,
          "duplicate_contact_id": null,
          "duplicate_ext_id": null,
          "duplicate_email_id": null,
          "duplicate_phone_id": null,
          "duplicate_whatsapp_id": null,
          "duplicate_landline_number_id": null

      "status": "completed",
      "export_url": "https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/api-export.example.com/upload/contacts_export.csv"
    },
    {
      "id": 212,
      "name": "IMPORTUSER",
      "status": "queued"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

## Get process details

<a id="opIdgetProcess"></a>

`GET /processes/{processId}`

Retrieves detailed information about a specific background process.

**Use this to:**
- Get detailed status of a specific process
- Monitor process progress and completion
- Download results from completed export processes
- Check error details for failed processes
- Track process execution times

**Key information returned:**
- Complete process details (ID, name, status)
- Download URLs for completed export processes
- Import details with CSV report URLs for completed import processes

**Important considerations:**
- Process ID must exist in your account and not be deleted
- Completed export processes include download URLs
- Completed import processes include CSV report URLs with details about problematic records
- Different process types return different result structures

<h1 id="brevo-api-senders">Senders</h1>

## Get email senders

<a id="opIdgetSenders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/senders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /senders`

Retrieves a list of all email senders from your Brevo account with optional filtering.

**Use this to:**
- Get all available senders for email campaign setup
- Find sender details including ID, name, and email address
- Filter senders by IP address for dedicated IP users
- Filter senders by domain for domain-specific configurations
- Monitor sender configuration and status

**Key information returned:**
- Sender details (ID, name, email address)
- Sender status and verification information
- Associated IP addresses and domains (for dedicated IP accounts)
- Sender configuration settings

**Important considerations:**
- Standard accounts show empty IP arrays, dedicated IP accounts show IP assignments
- Filtering by IP only available for accounts with dedicated IPs
- Domain filtering helps organize senders by business units or brands
- Sender status indicates if sender is active and ready for campaign use
- Email verification required before sender can be used in campaigns


<h3 id="get-email-senders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ip|query|string|false|Filter your senders for a specific ip. **Available for dedicated IP usage only**<br>|
|domain|query|string|false|Filter your senders for a specific domain|

```json
  "senders": [
    {
      "active": true,
      "email": "support@example.com",
      "id": 1,
      "ips": [],

}
```

## Create email sender

<a id="opIdcreateSender"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/senders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "support@example.com",
    "name": "Support Team"
  }'
```

`POST /senders`

Creates a new email sender in your Brevo account.

**Use this to:**
- Add new senders for email campaigns
- Configure sender identity (name and email)
- Associate dedicated IPs with the sender (for dedicated IP accounts)
- Set up domain-based sender configurations

**Key information returned:**
- Created sender ID
- DKIM and SPF configuration status
- Success confirmation

**Important considerations:**
- Verification email sent to specified sender address
- DKIM and SPF configuration affects deliverability
- Dedicated IP accounts require IP association during creation
- IP weights must sum to 100 when specified
- Sender must be verified before use in campaigns


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "support@example.com",
  "name": "Support Team"
}
```

<h3 id="create-email-sender-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|sender's configuration|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|From email to use for the sender. A verification email will be<br>sent to this address.|
|» ips|body|[object]|false|**Mandatory in case of dedicated IP**. IPs to associate to the<br>sender. Not required for standard accounts.|
|» » domain|body|string|true|Domain of the IP|
|» » ip|body|string|true|Dedicated IP available in your account|
|» » weight|body|integer(int64)|false|Weight to apply to the IP. Sum of all IP weights must be<br>100. Should be passed for either ALL or NONE of the IPs.<br>If it's not passed, the sending will be equally balanced<br>on all IPs.|
|» name|body|string|true|From Name to use for the sender|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 15,
  "dkimError": false,
  "spfError": false
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

## Update a sender

<a id="opIdupdateSender"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/senders/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "New Support Team"
  }'
```

`PUT /senders/{senderId}`

Updates an existing email sender's configuration.

Use this to:
- Modify sender display name or email address
- Update dedicated IP associations
- Change sender configuration settings
- Correct sender information

Key information returned:
- Success confirmation
- Updated sender details

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "New Support Team"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|senderId|path|integer(int64)|true|Id of the sender|

|» email|body|string(email)|false|From Email to update the sender|
|» ips|body|[object]|false|**Only in case of dedicated IP**. IPs to associate to the<br>sender. If passed, will replace all the existing IPs. Not required for standard accounts.|

|» » ip|body|string|true|Dedicated IP available in your account|
|» » weight|body|integer(int64)|false|Weight to apply to the IP. Sum of all IP weights must be<br>100. Should be passed for either ALL or NONE of the IPs.<br>If it's not passed, the sending will be equally balanced<br>on all IPs.|

## Get a sender domain configuration

<a id="opIdgetDomainConfiguration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/senders/domains/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /senders/domains/{domainName}`

Retrieves configuration of a specific domain, to know if the domain is valid or not.

Use this to:
- Check domain configuration
- Validate a domain configuration
- Monitor DNS record status
- Troubleshoot authentication issues

Key information returned:
- Domain verification and authentication status
- DNS records configuration and validation status
- Detailed authentication requirements

<h3 id="get-a-sender-domain-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

```json
  "verified": true,
  "authenticated": true,
  "dns_records": {
    "brevo_code": {
      "host_name": "@",
      "type": "TXT",
      "value": "brevo-code=abc123def456",
      "status": true

    "dkim_record": {
```

<h1 id="brevo-api-webhooks">Webhooks</h1>

## Get all webhooks

<a id="opIdgetWebhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/webhooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /webhooks`

Retrieves all webhooks from your Brevo account with filtering and sorting options.

Use this to:
- Monitor webhook configurations and event handling
- List webhooks by type (transactional, marketing, inbound)
- Review webhook endpoints and authentication
- Track webhook creation and modification history
- Audit webhook event subscriptions

Key information returned:
- Complete webhook details and configuration
- Event types and channel subscriptions
- Authentication and security settings
- Webhook URLs and custom headers
- Creation and modification timestamps

<h3 id="get-all-webhooks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|query|string|false|Filter on webhook type|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of webhook creation|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|marketing|
|type|transactional|
|type|inbound|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

> Example responses

```json
    {
      "auth": {
        "token": "test-auth-token1234",

      "url": "http://exmaple.domain.com/15kxxxxxn1"

  ]
}
```

## Create a webhook

<a id="opIdcreateWebhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "auth": {
      "token": "test-auth-token1234",
      "type": "bearer"
    },
    "batched": true,
    "channel": "email",
    "description": "Webhook triggered on unsubscription",
    "domain": "example.com",
    "events": [
      "unsubscribed"
    ],
    "headers": [
      {
        "key": "cf-secret",
        "value": "test-header-value"
      }
    ],
    "type": "marketing",
    "url": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1"
  }'
```

`POST /webhooks`

Creates a new webhook to receive real-time notifications for specified events.

Use this to:
- Set up event notifications for transactional or marketing emails
- Configure webhook endpoints for campaign tracking
- Enable real-time monitoring of email delivery status
- Subscribe to contact list changes and updates
- Implement custom event handling and automation

Key information returned:
- Created webhook ID and configuration
- Success confirmation and setup details

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auth": {
    "token": "test-auth-token1234",
    "type": "bearer"
  },
  "batched": true,
  "channel": "email",
  "description": "Webhook triggered on unsubscription",
  "domain": "example.com",
  "events": [
    "unsubscribed"
  ],
  "headers": [
    {
      "key": "cf-secret",
      "value": "test-header-value"
    }
  ],
  "type": "marketing",
  "url": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to create a webhook|
|» auth|body|object|false|Add authentication on webhook url|
|» » token|body|string|false|Webhook authentication token|
|» » type|body|string|false|Type of authentication|
|» batched|body|boolean|false|To send batched webhooks|
|» channel|body|string|false|Channel of the webhook|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the webhook|
|» domain|body|string|false|Inbound domain of webhook, required in case of event type<br>`inbound`|
|» events|body|[string]|false|Events triggering the webhook. Required for transactional and<br>marketing types, optional for inbound type (defaults to<br>`inboundEmailProcessed`). Possible values for **Transactional**<br>type webhook: `sent` OR `request`, `delivered`, `hardBounce`,<br>`softBounce`, `blocked`, `spam`, `invalid`, `deferred`, `click`,<br>`opened`, `uniqueOpened` and `unsubscribed`. Possible values for<br>**Marketing** type webhook: `spam`, `opened`, `click`,<br>`hardBounce`, `softBounce`, `unsubscribed`, `listAddition`,<br>`delivered`, `contactUpdated` & `contactDeleted`. Possible values<br>for **Inbound** type webhook: `inboundEmailProcessed`.|
|» headers|body|[object]|false|Custom headers to be send with webhooks|
|» » key|body|string|false|Header key name|
|» » value|body|string|false|Header value|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of the webhook|
|» url|body|string(url)|true|URL of the webhook|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

|» channel|sms|
|» events|sent|

|» events|softBounce|

|» events|invalid|
|» events|deferred|

|» events|uniqueOpened|
|» events|unsubscribed|
|» events|listAddition|
|» events|contactUpdated|
|» events|contactDeleted|
|» events|inboundEmailProcessed|
|» events|reply|
|» type|transactional|
|» type|marketing|
|» type|inbound|

## Export webhook event history as CSV file

<a id="opIdexportWebhooksHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/webhooks/export \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "days": 7,
    "email": "example@brevo.com",
    "endDate": "2023-02-17",
    "event": "request",
    "messageId": "<23befbae-1505-47a8-bd27-e30ef739f32c@fr.sib>",
    "notifyURL": "https://brevo.com",
    "sort": "desc",
    "startDate": "2023-02-13",
    "type": "transactional",
    "webhookId": 2345
  }'
```

`POST /webhooks/export`

<Note>This is an enterprise feature.

To have it activated please send us a request and we will activate it for your account.</Note>

Exports webhook event history to CSV format for analysis and reporting.

Use this to:
- Generate comprehensive webhook event reports
- Analyze webhook delivery patterns and success rates
- Export event data for external analysis tools
- Create historical reports for compliance and auditing
- Track webhook performance and reliability metrics

Key information returned:
- Process ID for tracking export completion
- CSV file will be delivered to specified webhook URL

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "days": 7,
  "email": "example@brevo.com",
  "endDate": "2023-02-17",
  "event": "request",
  "messageId": "<23befbae-1505-47a8-bd27-e30ef739f32c@fr.sib>",
  "notifyURL": "https://brevo.com",
  "sort": "desc",
  "startDate": "2023-02-13",
  "type": "transactional",
  "webhookId": 2345
}
```

<h3 id="export-webhook-event-history-as-csv-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to submit for webhooks history|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» days|body|integer|false|Number of days in the past including today (positive<br>integer). _Not compatible with 'startDate' and 'endDate'_|
|» email|body|string|false|Filter the history for a specific email|
|» endDate|body|string|false|Mandatory if startDate is used. Ending date of the report<br>(YYYY-MM-DD). Must be greater than equal to startDate|
|» event|body|string|true|Filter the history for a specific event type|
|» messageId|body|string|false|Filter the history for a specific message id. Applicable<br>only for transactional webhooks.|
|» notifyURL|body|string|true|Webhook URL to receive CSV file link|
|» sort|body|string|false|Sorting order of records (asc or desc)|
|» startDate|body|string|false|Mandatory if endDate is used. Starting date of the history<br>(YYYY-MM-DD). Must be lower than equal to endDate|
|» type|body|string|true|Filter the history based on webhook type|
|» webhookId|body|integer|false|Filter the history for a specific webhook id|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» event|invalid_parameter|
|» event|missing_parameter|

## Update a webhook

<a id="opIdupdateWebhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/webhooks/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "auth": {
      "token": "test-auth-token1234",
      "type": "bearer"
    },
    "batched": true,
    "description": "Webhook triggered on contact hardbounce",
    "domain": "example.com",
    "events": [
      "hardBounce"
    ],
    "headers": [
      {
        "key": "cf-secret",
        "value": "test-header-value"
      }
    ],
    "url": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1"
  }'
```

`PUT /webhooks/{webhookId}`

Updates an existing webhook configuration and event subscriptions.

Use this to:
- Modify webhook event subscriptions and triggers
- Update webhook URL and endpoint configuration
- Change authentication settings and credentials
- Adjust custom headers and request parameters
- Enable or disable specific webhook events

Key information returned:
- Success confirmation of webhook updates

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auth": {
    "token": "test-auth-token1234",
    "type": "bearer"
  },
  "batched": true,
  "description": "Webhook triggered on contact hardbounce",
  "domain": "example.com",
  "events": [
    "hardBounce"
  ],
  "headers": [
    {
      "key": "cf-secret",
      "value": "test-header-value"
    }
  ],
  "url": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1"
}
```

|» » token|body|string|false|Webhook authentication token|
|» » type|body|string|false|Type of authentication|

## Delete a webhook

<a id="opIddeleteWebhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/webhooks/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

`DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}`

Permanently deletes a webhook and stops all event notifications.

Use this to:
- Remove unused or obsolete webhook configurations
- Clean up webhook endpoints and subscriptions
- Stop event notifications to specific URLs
- Maintain organized webhook management

Key information returned:

<h1 id="brevo-api-external-feeds">External Feeds</h1>

## Get all external feeds

<a id="opIdgetAllExternalFeeds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/feeds \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /feeds`

Retrieves all external feeds from your Brevo account with filtering and pagination.

**Use this to:**
- Get an overview of all external data feeds
- Find feeds by name using search functionality
- Filter feeds by creation date range
- Browse feeds by authentication type
- Monitor feed library organization and usage

**Key information returned:**
- Feed details (UUID, name, URL, authentication type)
- Feed configuration and settings
- Creation and modification timestamps
- Feed status and error information
- Authentication and header configurations

**Important considerations:**
- External feeds enable dynamic content in email campaigns
- Feeds must be accessible from Brevo servers
- Authentication credentials are securely stored
- Feed performance affects campaign delivery
- Use pagination for accounts with many feeds
- Date range filtering limited to 30 days maximum
- Search functionality works on feed name matching
- Internal feeds are system-managed and cannot be modified


<h3 id="get-all-external-feeds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|search|query|string|false|Can be used to filter records by search keyword on feed name|
|startDate|query|string(date)|false|Mandatory if `endDate` is used. Starting date (YYYY-MM-DD) from which<br>you want to fetch the list. Can be maximum 30 days older than current<br>date.|
|endDate|query|string(date)|false|Mandatory if `startDate` is used. Ending date (YYYY-MM-DD) till which<br>you want to fetch the list. Maximum time period that can be selected is<br>one month.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation.<br>Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed.|
|authType|query|string|false|Filter the records by `authType` of the feed.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents returned per page.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document on the page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|
|authType|basic|
|authType|token|
|authType|noAuth|

## Create external feed

<a id="opIdcreateExternalFeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/feeds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Public API Feed",
    "url": "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts",
    "authType": "noAuth",
    "cache": true,
    "maxRetries": 3
  }'
```

`POST /feeds`

Creates a new external feed for dynamic content in email campaigns.

**Use this to:**
- Set up external data sources for dynamic content
- Configure authentication for protected feeds
- Enable real-time content updates in campaigns
- Establish connections to product catalogs, blogs, or APIs

**Key information returned:**
- Created feed UUID for reference in campaigns
- Success confirmation

**Important considerations:**
- Feed URL must be accessible from Brevo infrastructure
- Authentication credentials are securely encrypted
- Test feed accessibility before campaign use
- Consider feed response time for campaign performance
- Monitor feed reliability and uptime
- Use caching for frequently accessed feeds
- Maximum 5 retry attempts allowed for failed requests
- Custom headers support for API integration requirements


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Public API Feed",
  "url": "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts",
  "authType": "noAuth",
  "cache": true,
  "maxRetries": 3
}
```

<h3 id="create-external-feed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|External feed configuration|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the feed|
|» url|body|string(url)|true|URL of the external data source|
|» authType|body|string|false|Authentication type for accessing the feed|
|» username|body|string|false|Username for basic authentication (required if authType is 'basic')|
|» password|body|string|false|Password for basic authentication (required if authType is 'basic')|
|» token|body|string|false|Token for token-based authentication (required if authType is 'token')|
|» maxRetries|body|integer|false|Maximum number of retry attempts for failed requests|
|» cache|body|boolean|false|Whether to cache the feed response|
|» headers|body|[object]|false|Custom HTTP headers for the feed request|
|» » name|body|string|true|Header name|
|» » value|body|string|true|Header value|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» authType|basic|
|» authType|token|
|» authType|noAuth|

`GET /feeds/{uuid}`

**Use this to:**

- Check feed authentication settings
- Review feed personalization options
- Verify feed URL and parameters
- Monitor feed modification history

**Key information returned:**
- Complete feed configuration and settings
- Authentication credentials and headers
- Personalization and fallback settings
- Creation and modification timestamps
- Cache and retry configurations

**Important considerations:**
- UUID must exist in your account
- Provides complete feed information for troubleshooting
- Essential before making modifications
- Shows current feed health status
- Useful for debugging feed issues

## Update external feed

<a id="opIdupdateExternalFeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/feeds/b1c2d3e4-f5a6-47b8-89c0-d1e2f3a4b5c6 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Updated Product Catalog",
    "url": "https://api.newstore.com/products/v2"
  }'
```

`PUT /feeds/{uuid}`

Updates configuration of an existing external feed.

**Use this to:**
- Update feed URLs when data sources change
- Modify authentication credentials
- Change cache and retry settings
- Update custom headers
- Rename feeds for better organization

**Key information returned:**
- Success confirmation message

**Important considerations:**
- Only provided fields will be updated
- Feed UUID must exist in your account
- Authentication changes require verification
- URL changes should be tested before campaign use
- Monitor campaigns using this feed after updates


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Updated Product Catalog",
  "url": "https://api.newstore.com/products/v2"
}
```

<h3 id="update-external-feed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|uuid|path|string(uuidv4)|true|UUID of the feed to update|
|body|body|object|true|Feed configuration updates|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the feed|
|» url|body|string(url)|false|URL of the external data source|
|» authType|body|string|false|Authentication type for accessing the feed|
|» username|body|string|false|Username for basic authentication|
|» password|body|string|false|Password for basic authentication|
|» token|body|string|false|Token for token-based authentication|
|» headers|body|[object]|false|Custom HTTP headers for the feed request|
|» » name|body|string|true|Header name|
|» » value|body|string|true|Header value|
|» maxRetries|body|integer|false|Maximum number of retry attempts for failed requests|
|» cache|body|boolean|false|Whether to cache the feed response|

|» authType|basic|
|» authType|token|

## Delete external feed

<a id="opIddeleteExternalFeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/feeds/b1c2d3e4-f5a6-47b8-89c0-d1e2f3a4b5c6 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /feeds/{uuid}`

Deletes an external feed from your Brevo account.

**Use this to:**
- Remove external feeds that are no longer needed
- Clean up unused data sources
- Remove test or outdated feeds
- Maintain organized feed library

**Key information returned:**
- Success confirmation message

**Important considerations:**
- This action is PERMANENT and cannot be undone
- Feed configuration and history will be lost
- Check if feed is used in active campaigns before deletion
- Remove feed references from email templates
- Consider deactivating instead of deleting if unsure

## Create/Update object records in bulk

<a id="opIdupsertrecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/objects/vehicle/batch/upsert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "records": [
      {
        "identifiers": {
          "ext_id": "VIN123"
        },
        "attributes": {
          "make": "Toyota",
          "model": "Camry",
          "year": 2020,
          "engine_type": "hybrid"
        },
        "associations": [
          {
            "object_type": "garage",
            "action": "link",
            "records": [
              {
                "identifiers": {
                  "id": 435435
                }
              }
            ]
          },
          {
            "object_type": "garage",
            "action": "unlink",
            "records": [
              {
                "identifiers": {
                  "ext_id": "old-garage-001"
                }
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /objects/{object_type}/batch/upsert`

<Note title="Enterprise access only">Custom objects are only available to Enterprise plans.
This feature is in beta. These are subject to change.</Note>
Performs bulk create or update (upsert) operations for object records in a single asynchronous request. This endpoint is optimized for high-volume data imports and synchronization scenarios.

**How Upsert Works:**
- **Create**: Omit `identifiers`, or provide only `ext_id` (if it doesn't already exist). A new record is created with a Brevo-generated `id`.
- **Update**: Provide `id` (Brevo internal ID) or an `ext_id` that already exists. The matching record is updated with the new attribute values.
- **Important:** `id` is for **updates only**. Providing an `id` that does not belong to an existing record will fail during async processing (the HTTP response will still be 202, but the record will be rejected in the background). To create a new record with a stable external reference, use `ext_id` instead.

**Request Structure:**
Each object record in the `records` array can include:
- `identifiers`: Either `id` (internal Brevo ID) or `ext_id` (your external system ID) — required for updates. **Note:** use `id` (singular), not `ids`.
- `attributes`: Key-value pairs where each key is the attribute **key** (e.g., `company_name`), not the attribute label (e.g., "Company Name").
- `associations`: Controls linking and unlinking of associated records (optional). Each entry specifies:
    - `object_type`: The type of the associated object
    - `action`: `link` (default) to create the association, or `unlink` to remove it
    - `records`: The associated records to link or unlink (each identified by `ext_id` or `id`)
    - **Unlink is idempotent** — unlinking a non-existing association is a no-op (no error returned)
    - `link` and `unlink` actions can be submitted for the same `object_type` in a single record entry
    - Both associated records must already exist before a link can be created

> **Common mistake:** Passing the attribute **label** (the display name you see in the UI) instead of the attribute **key** will cause the attribute to be silently ignored and the record may not be created as expected.

**Asynchronous Processing:**
- Returns immediately with a `processId` (HTTP 202 Accepted)
- Use the processId to track status via the Get process API

**API and Schema Limitations:**
- Max 1000 object records per request
- Max request body size: 1 MB
- Max 500 attributes per object record (matches the schema limit of 500 attributes per object)
- Unknown attribute keys are silently ignored (no error, no attribute creation)
- Max 10 association records per associated object-type in each record of the request. If you need more, send multiple requests.

**Important Behaviors:**
- The object schema must be created before upserting records
- Unknown attribute keys are silently ignored (no error, no creation)
- Both associated object records must already exist before creating a link association
- Unlink operations are idempotent: attempting to unlink a non-existing association returns success
- `link` and `unlink` actions can be submitted for the same `object_type` in a single record entry
- Contact objects cannot be created via this endpoint
- For `category` and `multiple_category` attributes, pass the option **key** as the value (not the option label or option ID).
- The `id` identifier (internal Brevo ID) can only be used for **updating** existing records. To create new records, either omit identifiers (Brevo auto-generates an ID) or provide an `ext_id`.

**Errors:**
- Make sure both object records exist before associating them, else the API will return an error.
- This route does not create objects. The object where the object records are upserted by this API must be created already else the API will return an error "invalid object type".

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "identifiers": {
        "ext_id": "VIN123"
      },
      "attributes": {
        "make": "Toyota",
        "model": "Camry",
        "year": 2020,
        "engine_type": "hybrid"
      },
      "associations": [
        {
          "object_type": "garage",
          "action": "link",
          "records": [
            {
              "identifiers": {
                "id": 435435
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "object_type": "garage",
          "action": "unlink",
          "records": [
            {
              "identifiers": {
                "ext_id": "old-garage-001"
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="createupdate-object-records-in-bulk-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object_type|path|string|true|Object type for the records to upsert. Must be a previously created custom object type. Only lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores are allowed (max 32 characters).|
|body|body|object|true|Payload for batch upsert object records with associations|
|» records|body|[object]|true|List of object records to be upsert. Each record can have attributes, identifiers, and associations.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » associations|body|[object]|false|List of associations for the object record. Maximum 20 total entries allowed, with a maximum of 10 link actions and 10 unlink actions. Each entry specifies an object_type and an action (link or unlink). Unlink is idempotent — removing a non-existing association does not return an error. Both associated records must already exist before creating a link.<br>|
|» » » object_type|body|string|true|Type of the associated object|
|» » » action|body|string|false|Action to perform on the association. - `link`: Create association between records (default if not provided) - `unlink`: Remove association between records. Idempotent — unlinking a non-existing association is a no-op success.<br>|
|» » » records|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » » » identifiers|body|object|false|Identifiers for the associated object record. Provide either `ext_id` or `id`.|
|» » » » » ext_id|body|string|false|External ID of the associated record in your system.|
|» » » » » id|body|integer|false|Internal ID of the associated object record generated by Brevo.|
|» » attributes|body|object|false|Key-value pairs of attribute data for the object record. Each key must be the attribute **key** (e.g., `company_name`, `engine_type`), not the attribute label (e.g., "Company Name", "Engine Type"). Only attributes that already exist in the object schema will be accepted — unknown keys are silently ignored. Minimum 1 attribute is required.<br><br>For `category` or `multiple_category` attributes, set the value to the option **key** (not the option label or option ID). You can find available option keys in the `options` array returned by the GET attributes endpoint, or in the frontend under each attribute's settings.<br><br>For example, use the option key "hybrid" not the label "Hybrid" — using the label will be silently ignored.<br><br>For `multiple_choice` type, pass an **array of option keys** (not display labels). For example, if options have keys `"sunroof"` and `"leather_seats"`, pass `["sunroof", "leather_seats"]`.<br>|
|» » identifiers|body|object|false|Identifiers for the object record. Supports `id` (singular, not `ids`) or `ext_id`.<br>- `ext_id`: Your external system's identifier for this record.<br>- `id`: Internal Brevo record ID — can only be used for **updating** existing records, not for creation.<br>NOTE:<br>- This is an optional field. If no identifier is provided, Brevo auto-generates an internal ID that you can use for future operations.<br>- If both `ext_id` and `id` are provided, `id` takes precedence and the operation is treated as an update. It is recommended to provide only one identifier per record.<br>|
|» » » ext_id|body|string|false|ext_id is ID of record in the external system that client wants to store in the object system.|
|» » » id|body|integer|false|Internal ID of the object record generated by Brevo|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » action|link|
|» » » action|unlink|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Batch object records are being processed",
  "processId": 21
}
```

<h3 id="createupdate-object-records-in-bulk-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Batch request accepted for processing of upsert object records.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request (e.g., invalid organization ID, invalid object_type, records cannot be empty or more than 1000)|None|
|403|Forbidden|Custom objects are not available on this account, or upsert of Brevo standard object records is not supported via this endpoint.|None|
|404|Not Found|Object not found for the provided organization or object type|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error|None|

<h3 id="createupdate-object-records-in-bulk-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string|false|none|none|
|processId|integer(int64)|false|none|Unique Id for the batch process used to track the status of the batch. **How to use this processId:**   Refer to the [Get process status API](https://developers.brevo.com/reference/get-process) to check the execution status of this batch using the returned `processId`.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api-key, partner-key
</aside>

## Get the list of object records and total records count for an object.

<a id="opIdgetrecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.brevo.com/v3/objects/vehicle/records?limit=0&page_num=1' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /objects/{object_type}/records`

<Note title="Enterprise access only">Custom objects are only available to Enterprise plans.
This feature is in beta. These are subject to change.</Note>
This API retrieves a list of object records along with their associated records and provides the total count of records for the specified object. **Note**: Contact as object type is not supported in this endpoint.

<h3 id="get-the-list-of-object-records-and-total-records-count-for-an-object-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|object_type|path|string|true|Object type for the records to retrieve. Must be a previously created custom object type. Contact as object type is not supported in this endpoint.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|true|Number of records returned per page|
|page_num|query|integer(int64)|true|Page number for pagination. It's used to fetch the object records on a provided page number. Must be a valid positive integer.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort order, must be 'asc' or 'desc'. Default to 'desc' if not provided.|
|association|query|string|false|Whether to include associations, must be 'true' or 'false'. Default to 'false' if not provided.|

|sort|desc|

## Delete multiple object records (up to 1000) asynchronously

<a id="opIdbatchDeleteObjectRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/objects/vehicle/batch/delete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "identifiers": {
      "ext_ids": [
        "ext-001",
        "ext-002"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /objects/{object_type}/batch/delete`

Use this endpoint to delete multiple object records of the same object-type in one request.
The request is accepted and processed asynchronously. You can track the status of the deletion process using the returned **processId**.
**Limitations:** - Each request can contain up to **1000** object record identifiers - Either `ids` or `ext_ids` must be provided, but **not both** in the same request - Deletion of Brevo standard object records is not supported via this endpoint - If more records must be deleted, send multiple batch requests


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "identifiers": {
    "ext_ids": [
      "ext-001",
      "ext-002"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-multiple-object-records-up-to-1000-asynchronously-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object_type|path|string|true|Object type for the records to delete|
|body|body|object|true|List of object record identifiers to delete|
|» identifiers|body|object|false|Either `ids` or `ext_ids` must be provided, but not both in the same request.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » ids|body|[integer]|true|List of object record IDs|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » ext_ids|body|[string]|true|List of external record identifiers|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "processId": 21,
  "message": "Batch object records are being processed for deletion"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-multiple-object-records-up-to-1000-asynchronously-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Batch request accepted for deletion - process started|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request (e.g., invalid object_type, invalid request body, both ids and ext_ids provided, or exceeds 1000 identifiers limit)|None|
|403|Forbidden|Deletion of Brevo standard object records is not supported via this endpoint|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error|None|

<h3 id="delete-multiple-object-records-up-to-1000-asynchronously-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|processId|integer(int64)|false|none|Identifier for batch process tracking|
|message|string|false|none|none|

<a id="opIdgetAssociatedRecords"></a>

`GET /objects/{object_type}/associated-records`

<Note title="Enterprise access only">Custom objects are only available to Enterprise plans.
This feature is in beta. These are subject to change.</Note>
Returns the records associated with a single source record. Associations of every type are returned together in one paginated list, ordered by association creation time with the most recently created association first.

**Identifying the source record**
Provide exactly one of `id`, `ext_id`, `email` or `sms`. Passing none of them, or more than one, returns `400`. `email` and `sms` are only accepted when `object_type` is `contact`; using either with any other object type returns `400`.

**Object types**
Use the object type exactly as it is defined in your account, for example `vehicle` for a custom object of that name, or `contact` for contacts. An object type that does not exist in your account returns `400`.

**Filtering by associated object type**
Use `type` to restrict the response to one or more associated object types, for example `?type=contact&type=garage`. Up to 5 types can be requested per call; more returns `400`. When `type` is omitted, associations of every type are returned.

**Pagination**
Results are returned 20 per page. The page size is fixed and cannot be changed. Increase `offset` by 20 to walk through the pages until `has_more` is `false`. An `offset` beyond the last record returns an empty `items` array with `has_more` set to `false`.

**Working with contacts**
- `contact` is supported both as the source `object_type` and as an associated object type.
- An `id`, `ext_id`, `email` or `sms` that matches no contact returns `404`.
- If several contacts share the same `ext_id`, `email` or `sms`, identify the contact by `id` to be sure of which one is used.
- Contacts returned in `items` carry all of the contact's attributes, with attribute keys in lowercase — `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `sms`, `ext_id`, and any other contact attribute lowercased.
- For contacts, `ext_id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` are not returned on `object`. A contact's external ID is available as `attributes.ext_id` when it is set.

<h3 id="get-the-records-associated-with-an-object-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object_type|path|string|true|Object type of the source record, exactly as defined in your account. Accepts any object type defined in the account, for example a custom object type or `contact`.|
|id|query|integer(int64)|false|Internal Brevo ID of the source record. Must be a positive integer. Provide exactly one of `id`, `ext_id`, `email` or `sms`.|
|ext_id|query|string|false|External ID of the source record in your system. Provide exactly one of `id`, `ext_id`, `email` or `sms`.|
|email|query|string|false|Email address of the source contact. Only accepted when `object_type` is `contact`. Provide exactly one of `id`, `ext_id`, `email` or `sms`.|
|sms|query|string|false|Phone number of the source contact, including the country code. It may be given with or without a leading `+`; percent-encode the `+` as `%2B`, because a literal `+` in a query string is read as a space. Only accepted when `object_type` is `contact`. Provide exactly one of `id`, `ext_id`, `email` or `sms`.|
|type|query|[string]|false|Restricts the response to the given associated object types. Repeat the parameter to request several types, for example `?type=contact&type=garage`. Maximum 5 types per call. Associations of every type are returned when omitted.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of records to skip before the first record of the page. Defaults to 0. Increase by 20 to fetch the next page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "type": "garage",
      "object": {
        "id": 12345,
        "ext_id": "f7e8d9c0ba",
        "attributes": {
          "name": "Downtown Motors",
          "city": "Paris"
        },
        "created_at": "2026-07-22T10:20:30Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-07-22T10:20:30Z"
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "contact",
      "object": {
        "id": 402,
        "attributes": {
          "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
          "first_name": "Jane",
          "last_name": "Doe",
          "ext_id": "crm-4471"
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "offset": 0,
  "has_more": true
}
```

<h3 id="get-the-records-associated-with-an-object-record-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A page of records associated with the source record.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request. Returned when none or several of `id`, `ext_id`, `email` and `sms` are provided, when `email` or `sms` is used with an `object_type` other than `contact`, when `id` or `offset` is not a valid value, when more than 5 values are passed to `type`, or when `object_type` or a `type` value is not an object type defined in the account.|None|
|404|Not Found|No record matches the provided `id`, `ext_id`, `email` or `sms` for this object type.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error|None|

<h3 id="get-the-records-associated-with-an-object-record-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|has_more|boolean|false|none|`true` when at least one more associated record exists after this page.|
|items|[object]|false|none|Associated records for this page, up to 20 per page. Fewer when the last page is reached, empty when the source record has no matching associations.|
|» object|object|false|none|The associated record. `ext_id`, `attributes`, `created_at` and `updated_at` are omitted when they are not available for the record.|
|» » attributes|object|false|none|Key-value pairs of attribute data for the associated record. Each key is the attribute **key** (e.g., `company_name`, `engine_type`), not the attribute label (e.g., "Company Name", "Engine Type").<br>For `category` or `multiple_category` attributes, the value is the option **key** (not the option label or option ID).<br>For contacts, attribute keys are returned in lowercase, for example `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `sms` and `ext_id`.<br>|
|» » created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the associated record was created. Not returned for contacts.|
|» » ext_id|string|false|none|External ID of the associated record in your system. Not returned for contacts, whose external ID is available as `attributes.ext_id`.|
|» » id|integer(int64)|false|none|Internal ID of the associated record generated by Brevo.|
|» » updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the associated record was last updated. Not returned for contacts.|
|» type|string|false|none|Object type of the associated record.|
|offset|integer(int64)|false|none|The offset that was requested.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api-key, partner-key
</aside>

<h1 id="brevo-api-contacts">Contacts</h1>

## Get all the contacts

<a id="opIdgetContacts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /contacts`

Retrieve all contacts from your Brevo account with support for pagination, filtering, and sorting. Results default to 50 contacts per page (maximum 1000) sorted in descending order of creation, and can be filtered by modification date, creation date, contact IDs (up to 20), list IDs, segment ID, or contact attributes using the equals operator. Note that either listIds or segmentId can be passed but not both simultaneously.

<h3 id="get-all-the-contacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document of the page|
|modifiedSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the contacts modified after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.**<br>|
|createdSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the contacts created after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.**<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|
|ids|query|[integer(int64)]|false|Filter by a list of contact IDs. You can pass a **maximum of 20 IDs**. All elements must be integers.|
|segmentId|query|integer(int64)|false|Id of the segment. **Either listIds or segmentId can be passed.** Must be a positive integer (minimum value of 1).|
|listIds|query|[integer(int64)]|false|Ids of the list. **Either listIds or segmentId can be passed.**|
|filter|query|string|false|Filter the contacts on the basis of attributes. **Allowed operator: equals. For multiple-choice options, the filter will apply an AND condition between the options. For category attributes, the filter will work with both id and value. (e.g. filter=equals(FIRSTNAME,"Antoine"), filter=equals(B1, true), filter=equals(DOB, "1989-11-23"), filter=equals(GENDER, "1"), filter=equals(GENDER, "MALE"), filter=equals(COUNTRY,"USA, INDIA")**<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

## Create a contact

<a id="opIdcreateContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "attributes": {
      "COUNTRIES": [
        "India",
        "China"
      ],
      "FNAME": "Elly",
      "LNAME": "Roger"
    },
    "email": "elly@example.com",
    "emailBlacklisted": false,
    "ext_id": "externalId",
    "listIds": [
      36
    ],
    "smsBlacklisted": false,
    "smtpBlacklistSender": [
      "user@example.com"
    ],
    "updateEnabled": false,
    "forceMerge": true,
    "getId": true
  }'
```

`POST /contacts`

<Note>Follow this format when passing a "SMS" phone number as an attribute.
Accepted Number Formats 91xxxxxxxxxx +91xxxxxxxxxx 0091xxxxxxxxxx</Note>
Creates new contacts on Brevo. Contacts can be created by passing either - <br><br> 1. email address of the contact (email_id),  <br> 2. phone number of the contact (to be passed as "SMS" field in "attributes" along with proper country code), For example- {"SMS":"+91xxxxxxxxxx"} or {"SMS":"0091xxxxxxxxxx"} <br> 3. ext_id <br>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "COUNTRIES": [
      "India",
      "China"
    ],
    "FNAME": "Elly",
    "LNAME": "Roger"
  },
  "email": "elly@example.com",
  "emailBlacklisted": false,
  "ext_id": "externalId",
  "listIds": [
    36
  ],
  "smsBlacklisted": false,
  "smtpBlacklistSender": [
    "user@example.com"
  ],
  "updateEnabled": false,
  "forceMerge": true,
  "getId": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to create a contact|
|» attributes|body|object|false|Pass the set of attributes and their values. The attribute's parameter should be passed in capital letter while creating a contact. Values that don't match the attribute type (e.g. text or string in a date attribute) will be ignored. **These attributes must be present in your Brevo account**. For eg: **{"FNAME":"Elly", "LNAME":"Roger", "COUNTRIES": ["India","China"]}**<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|number \| string \| boolean \| [string]|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» email|body|string(email)|false|Email address of the user. **Mandatory if "ext_id"  & "SMS" field is not passed.**<br>|
|» emailBlacklisted|body|boolean|false|Set this field to blacklist the contact for emails (emailBlacklisted = true)|
|» ext_id|body|string|false|Pass your own Id to create a contact.|
|» listIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Ids of the lists to add the contact to|
|» smsBlacklisted|body|boolean|false|Set this field to blacklist the contact for SMS (smsBlacklisted = true)|
|» smtpBlacklistSender|body|[string(email)]|false|transactional email forbidden sender for contact. Use only for email Contact ( only available if updateEnabled = true )|
|» updateEnabled|body|boolean|false|Facilitate to update the existing contact in the same request (updateEnabled = true)|
|» forceMerge|body|boolean|false|When true, if the contact being created shares an identifier (email, SMS, ext_id, whatsapp, landline) with an existing contact, the two contacts are force-merged. The contact with the most recent `last_modified` timestamp is retained; the other is deleted. When false (default), a 4xx error is returned on identifier conflict.|
|» getId|body|boolean|false|When true, the response returns the `id` of the surviving contact after merge.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 21
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "duplicate_parameter",
  "message": "email is already associated with another Contact",
  "metadata": {
    "duplicate_identifiers": [
      "email"
    ]
  }
}
```

> 425 Response

```json
{
  "code": "duplicate_parameter",
  "message": "email is already associated with another Contact",
  "metadata": {
    "duplicate_identifiers": [
      "email"
    ]
  }
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
