|201|Created|Contact created|Inline|
|204|No Content|Contact updated|None|

|425|Too Early|Too Early|[contactErrorModel](#schemacontacterrormodel)|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

`GET /contacts/attributes`

Retrieve all contact attributes defined in your Brevo account, grouped by category (normal, transactional, category, calculated, global). ## Update contact attribute

<a id="opIdupdateAttribute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/attributes/category/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "enumeration": [
      {
        "label": "Men",
        "value": 1
      }
    ],
    "multiCategoryOptions": [
      "string"
    ],
    "value": "COUNT[BLACKLISTED,BLACKLISTED,<,NOW()]"
  }'
```

`PUT /contacts/attributes/{attributeCategory}/{attributeName}`

Update an existing contact attribute identified by its category and name. For category-type attributes, you can update the enumeration values; for calculated or global attributes, update the computed value formula; and for normal multiple-choice attributes, update the multicategory options. None of the category or multicategory option values can exceed 200 characters.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enumeration": [
    {
      "label": "Men",
      "value": 1
    }
  ],
  "multiCategoryOptions": [
    "string"
  ],
  "value": "COUNT[BLACKLISTED,BLACKLISTED,<,NOW()]"
}
```

<h3 id="update-contact-attribute-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attributeCategory|path|string|true|Category of the attribute|
|attributeName|path|string|true|Name of the existing attribute|
|body|body|object|true|Values to update an attribute|
|» enumeration|body|[object]|false|List of the values and labels that the attribute can take. **Use only if the attribute's category is "category"** None of the category options can exceed max 200 characters. For example, **[{"value":1, "label":"male"}, {"value":2, "label":"female"}]**<br>|
|» » label|body|string|true|Label of the value|
|» » value|body|integer|true|Id of the value|

## Create contact attribute

<a id="opIdcreateAttribute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/attributes/normal/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "enumeration": [
      {
        "label": "Women",
        "value": 1
      }
    ],
    "isRecurring": true,
    "multiCategoryOptions": [
      "string"
    ],
    "type": "text",
    "value": "COUNT[BLACKLISTED,BLACKLISTED,<,NOW()]"
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/attributes/{attributeCategory}/{attributeName}`

Create a new contact attribute under the specified category and name. The required body properties depend on the category: use "type" for normal, transactional, or category attributes; use "value" for calculated or global attributes; use "enumeration" for category attributes; and use "multiCategoryOptions" for normal multiple-choice attributes. None of the category or multicategory option values can exceed 200 characters.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enumeration": [
    {
      "label": "Women",
      "value": 1
    }
  ],
  "isRecurring": true,
  "multiCategoryOptions": [
    "string"
  ],
  "type": "text",
  "value": "COUNT[BLACKLISTED,BLACKLISTED,<,NOW()]"
}
```

<h3 id="create-contact-attribute-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attributeCategory|path|string|true|Category of the attribute|
|attributeName|path|string|true|Name of the attribute|
|body|body|object|true|Values to create an attribute|
|» enumeration|body|[object]|false|List of values and labels that the attribute can take. **Use only if the attribute's category is "category"**. None of the category options can exceed max 200 characters. For example: **[{"value":1, "label":"male"}, {"value":2, "label":"female"}]**<br>|
|» » label|body|string|true|Label of the value|
|» » value|body|integer|true|Id of the value|
|» isRecurring|body|boolean|false|Type of the attribute. **Use only if the attribute's category is 'calculated' or 'global'**<br>|
|» multiCategoryOptions|body|[string]|false|List of options you want to add for multiple-choice attribute. **Use only if the attribute's category is "normal" and attribute's type is "multiple-choice". None of the multicategory options can exceed max 200 characters.** For example: **["USA","INDIA"]**<br>|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of the attribute. **Use only if the attribute's category is 'normal', 'category' or 'transactional'** Type **user and multiple-choice** is only available if the category is **normal** attribute Type **id** is only available if the category is **transactional** attribute Type **category** is only available if the category is **category** attribute<br>|
|» value|body|string|false|Value of the attribute. **Use only if the attribute's category is 'calculated' or 'global'**<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|attributeCategory|normal|
|attributeCategory|transactional|
|attributeCategory|category|
|attributeCategory|calculated|
|attributeCategory|global|
|» type|text|
|» type|date|
|» type|float|
|» type|boolean|
|» type|id|
|» type|category|
|» type|multiple-choice|
|» type|user|

## Update multiple contacts

<a id="opIdupdateBatchContacts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "contacts": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "EMAIL": "newemail@domain.com",
          "FNAME": "Ellie",
          "LNAME": "Roger"
        },
        "email": "elly@example.com",
        "emailBlacklisted": false,
        "ext_id": "UpdateExternalId",
        "id": 31,
        "listIds": [
          65
        ],
        "sms": "+91xxxxxxxxxx",
        "smsBlacklisted": true,
        "smtpBlacklistSender": [
          "user@example.com"
        ],
        "unlinkListIds": [
          36
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/batch`

Update multiple contacts in a single API call by passing an array of contact objects. Each contact in the array must be identified by one of: email, id, or sms (only one identifier per contact). You can update attributes, blacklist status, list memberships, ext_id, and transactional email forbidden senders for each contact in the batch.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "contacts": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "EMAIL": "newemail@domain.com",
        "FNAME": "Ellie",
        "LNAME": "Roger"
      },
      "email": "elly@example.com",
      "emailBlacklisted": false,
      "ext_id": "UpdateExternalId",
      "id": 31,
      "listIds": [
        65
      ],
      "sms": "+91xxxxxxxxxx",
      "smsBlacklisted": true,
      "smtpBlacklistSender": [
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "unlinkListIds": [
        36
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-multiple-contacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to update multiple contacts|
|» contacts|body|[object]|false|List of contacts to be updated|
|» » attributes|body|object|false|Pass the set of attributes to be updated. **These attributes must be present in your account**. To update existing email address of a contact with the new one please pass EMAIL in attribtes. For example, **{ "EMAIL":"newemail@domain.com", "FNAME":"Ellie", "LNAME":"Roger"}**. Keep in mind transactional attributes can be updated the same way as normal attributes. Mobile Number in **SMS** field should be passed with proper country code. For example: **{"SMS":"+91xxxxxxxxxx"} or {"SMS":"0091xxxxxxxxxx"}**<br>|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|Email address of the user to be updated (For each operation only pass one of the supported contact identifiers. Email, id or sms)|
|» » emailBlacklisted|body|boolean|false|Set/unset this field to blacklist/allow the contact for emails (emailBlacklisted = true)|
|» » ext_id|body|string|false|Pass your own Id to update ext_id of a contact.|
|» » id|body|integer(int64)|false|id of the user to be updated (For each operation only pass one of the supported contact identifiers. Email, id or sms)|
|» » listIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Ids of the lists to add the contact to|
|» » sms|body|string|false|SMS of the user to be updated (For each operation only pass one of the supported contact identifiers. Email, id or sms)|
|» » smsBlacklisted|body|boolean|false|Set/unset this field to blacklist/allow the contact for SMS (smsBlacklisted = true)|
|» » smtpBlacklistSender|body|[string(email)]|false|transactional email forbidden sender for contact. Use only for email Contact|
|» » unlinkListIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Ids of the lists to remove the contact from|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

|400|Bad Request|bad request|Inline|

## Create Contact via DOI (Double-Opt-In) Flow

<a id="opIdcreateDoiContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/doubleOptinConfirmation \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "attributes": {
      "COUNTRIES": [
        "India",
        "China"
      ],
      "FNAME": "Elly",
      "LNAME": "Roger"
    },
    "contactPixelTrackingConsent": true,
    "email": "elly@example.com",
    "excludeListIds": [
      36
    ],
    "includeListIds": [
      36
    ],
    "redirectionUrl": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1",
    "templateId": 2
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/doubleOptinConfirmation`

<Note title="How to use attributes param?">attributes param in this endpoint is an object containing key-value pairs where values can be either a string, integer, array, or boolean. You can create key-value pairs with these four datatypes. When a value is an array, it should be an array of strings.</Note>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "COUNTRIES": [
      "India",
      "China"
    ],
    "FNAME": "Elly",
    "LNAME": "Roger"
  },
  "contactPixelTrackingConsent": true,
  "email": "elly@example.com",
  "excludeListIds": [
    36
  ],
  "includeListIds": [
    36
  ],
  "redirectionUrl": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1",
  "templateId": 2
}
```

<h3 id="create-contact-via-doi-double-opt-in-flow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to create the Double opt-in (DOI) contact|
|» attributes|body|object|false|Pass the set of attributes and their values. **These attributes must be present in your Brevo account**. For eg. **{'FNAME':'Elly', 'LNAME':'Roger', 'COUNTRIES': ['India','China']}**<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|number \| string \| boolean \| [string]|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» contactPixelTrackingConsent|body|boolean|false|Consent of the DOI recipient for open (pixel) and click tracking in the double opt-in confirmation email, resolved by the sender at send time. Considered only if the per-contact pixel tracking consent feature is enabled for your account. Pass `true` if this recipient has consented to open and click tracking, in which case the open pixel and tracked links identify the recipient. Pass `false` to anonymise the open and click events (counted in aggregate statistics only). If it is not passed, the recipient is treated as unknown consent status and the email is still sent (the open and click are anonymised unless your account tracks unknown-consent contacts). A value other than `true`/`false` is rejected. Ignored when the feature is not enabled for your account.<br>|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|Email address where the confirmation email will be sent. This email address will be the identifier for all other contact attributes.|
|» excludeListIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Lists under user account where contact should not be added|
|» includeListIds|body|[integer(int64)]|true|Lists under user account where contact should be added|
|» redirectionUrl|body|string(url)|true|URL of the web page that user will be redirected to after clicking on the double opt in URL. When editing your DOI template you can reference this URL by using the tag **{{ params.DOIurl }}**.<br>|
|» templateId|body|integer(int64)|true|Id of the Double opt-in (DOI) template|

```json
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

## Export contacts

<a id="opIdrequestContactExport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/export \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "customContactFilter": {
      "actionForContacts": "allContacts",
      "actionForEmailCampaigns": "openers",
      "actionForSmsCampaigns": "hardBounces",
      "createdSince": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "emailCampaignId": 12,
      "listId": 2,
      "modifiedSince": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "segmentId": 2,
      "smsCampaignId": 12
    },
    "disableNotification": false,
    "exportAttributes": [
      "NAME"
    ],
    "exportMandatoryAttributes": false,
    "exportMetadata": [
      "_listIds"
    ],
    "exportDateInUTC": true,
    "exportSubscriptionStatus": [
      "email_marketing"
    ],
    "notifyUrl": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1"
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/export`

It returns the background process ID which on completion calls the notify URL that you have set in the input. File will be available in csv.

When no contact matches the filter, no export process is created: the endpoint answers `200` with an empty object instead of `202` with a processId. A recurring export should treat that as "nothing to do" rather than as a failure, and must not assume a processId is always present.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "customContactFilter": {
    "actionForContacts": "allContacts",
    "actionForEmailCampaigns": "openers",
    "actionForSmsCampaigns": "hardBounces",
    "createdSince": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "emailCampaignId": 12,
    "listId": 2,
    "modifiedSince": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "segmentId": 2,
    "smsCampaignId": 12
  },
  "disableNotification": false,
  "exportAttributes": [
    "NAME"
  ],
  "exportMandatoryAttributes": false,
  "exportMetadata": [
    "_listIds"
  ],
  "exportDateInUTC": true,
  "exportSubscriptionStatus": [
    "email_marketing"
  ],
  "notifyUrl": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1"
}
```

<h3 id="export-contacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to request a contact export|
|» customContactFilter|body|object|true|Set the filter for the contacts to be exported.<br>|
|» » actionForContacts|body|string|false|**Mandatory if neither actionForEmailCampaigns nor actionForSmsCampaigns is passed.** This will export the contacts on the basis of the provided action, restricted to the contacts selected by the other filters below. * **allContacts** - Fetch all the selected contacts. * **subscribed & unsubscribed** - Fetch the subscribed / unsubscribed (blacklisted via any means) contacts among the selected contacts. * **unsubscribedPerList** - Fetch the contacts that are unsubscribed from the given listId only; this action requires listId.<br><br>The selection must be narrowed by at least one of **listId**, **segmentId**, **modifiedSince** or **createdSince**. Any of them can be combined with the action, so for example `unsubscribed` together with `modifiedSince` exports the contacts that are currently blocklisted and were modified after the given date-time, with no list or segment involved.<br>|
|» » actionForEmailCampaigns|body|string|false|**Mandatory if neither actionForContacts nor actionForSmsCampaigns is passed.** This will export the contacts on the basis of provided action applied on email campaigns. * **openers & nonOpeners** - emailCampaignId is mandatory. Fetch the list of readers / non-readers for a particular email campaign. * **clickers & nonClickers** - emailCampaignId is mandatory. Fetch the list of clickers / non-clickers for a particular email campaign. * **unsubscribed** - emailCampaignId is mandatory. Fetch the list of all unsubscribed (blacklisted via any means) contacts for a particular email campaign. * **hardBounces & softBounces** - emailCampaignId is optional. Fetch the list of hard bounces / soft bounces for a particular / all email campaign(s).<br>|
|» » actionForSmsCampaigns|body|string|false|**Mandatory if neither actionForContacts nor actionForEmailCampaigns is passed.** This will export the contacts on the basis of provided action applied on sms campaigns. * **unsubscribed** - Fetch the list of all unsubscribed (blacklisted via any means) contacts for all / particular sms campaigns. * **hardBounces & softBounces** - Fetch the list of hard bounces / soft bounces for all / particular sms campaigns.<br>|
|» » createdSince|body|string(date-time)|false|Considered only if **actionForContacts** is passed, ignored otherwise. Exports only the contacts created after the given date-time. The value must be a full RFC 3339 date-time: a date-only value such as `2026-10-01` is rejected, and so is a value without a timezone, so pass either the `Z` suffix or an explicit `+HH:MM` offset.<br>|
|» » emailCampaignId|body|integer(int64)|false|Considered only if **actionForEmailCampaigns** is passed, ignored otherwise. **Mandatory if action is one of the following - openers, nonOpeners, clickers, nonClickers, unsubscribed.** The id of the email campaign for which the corresponding action shall be applied in the filter.<br>|
|» » listId|body|integer(int64)|false|ID of the list. Considered only if **actionForContacts** is passed. At least one of listId, segmentId, modifiedSince or createdSince must be provided; listId and segmentId cannot be used together.<br>|
|» » modifiedSince|body|string(date-time)|false|Considered only if **actionForContacts** is passed, ignored otherwise. Exports only the contacts modified after the given date-time. The value must be a full RFC 3339 date-time: a date-only value such as `2026-10-01` is rejected, and so is a value without a timezone, so pass either the `Z` suffix or an explicit `+HH:MM` offset. Note that a contact's modification date changes on any update, not only on a subscription change.<br>|
|» » segmentId|body|integer(int64)|false|ID of the segment. Considered only if **actionForContacts** is passed. At least one of listId, segmentId, modifiedSince or createdSince must be provided; listId and segmentId cannot be used together.<br>|
|» » smsCampaignId|body|integer(int64)|false|Considered only if **actionForSmsCampaigns** is passed, ignored otherwise. The id of sms campaign for which the corresponding action shall be applied in the filter.<br>|
|» disableNotification|body|boolean|false|To avoid generating the email notification upon contact export, pass **true**|
|» exportAttributes|body|[string]|false|List of all the attributes that you want to export. **These attributes must be present in your contact database. It is required if exportMandatoryAttributes is set false. ** For example: **['fname', 'lname', 'email']**<br>|
|» exportMandatoryAttributes|body|boolean|false|To export mandatory attributes like EMAIL, ADDED_TIME, MODIFIED_TIME|
|» exportMetadata|body|[string]|false|Export metadata of contacts such as _listIds, ADDED_TIME, MODIFIED_TIME.|
|» exportDateInUTC|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether the date fields createdAt, modifiedAt in the exported data should be returned in UTC format.|
|» exportSubscriptionStatus|body|[string]|false|Export subscription status of contacts for email & sms marketting. Pass email_marketing to obtain the marketing email subscription status & sms_marketing to retrieve the marketing SMS status of the contact.|
|» notifyUrl|body|string(url)|false|Webhook that will be called once the export process is finished. For reference, https://help.brevo.com/hc/en-us/articles/360007666479|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » actionForContacts|allContacts|
|» » actionForContacts|subscribed|
|» » actionForContacts|unsubscribed|
|» » actionForContacts|unsubscribedPerList|
|» » actionForEmailCampaigns|openers|
|» » actionForEmailCampaigns|nonOpeners|
|» » actionForEmailCampaigns|clickers|
|» » actionForEmailCampaigns|nonClickers|
|» » actionForEmailCampaigns|unsubscribed|
|» » actionForEmailCampaigns|hardBounces|
|» » actionForEmailCampaigns|softBounces|
|» » actionForSmsCampaigns|hardBounces|
|» » actionForSmsCampaigns|softBounces|
|» » actionForSmsCampaigns|unsubscribed|

## Update a folder

<a id="opIdupdateFolder"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/folders/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Wordpress Contacts"
  }'
```

`PUT /contacts/folders/{folderId}`

Update the name of an existing folder identified by its ID. The new folder name must be provided in the request body. Returns a 404 error if the folder ID does not exist.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Wordpress Contacts"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|folderId|path|integer(int64)|true|Id of the folder|
|body|body|[createUpdateFolder](#schemacreateupdatefolder)|true|Name of the folder|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the folder|

## Import contacts

<a id="opIdimportContacts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "disableNotification": false,
    "emailBlacklist": false,
    "emptyContactsAttributes": true,
    "fileBody": "NAME;SURNAME;EMAIL\nSmith;John;john.smith@example.com\nRoger;Ellie;ellie36@example.com",
    "fileUrl": "https://importfile.domain.com",
    "jsonBody": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "BIRTHDAY": "11/02/1989",
          "COUNTRY": "DE",
          "FNAME": "Dicky",
          "LANDLINE_NUMBER": "33689965433",
          "LNAME": "Noemi",
          "PREFERED_COLOR": "BLACK",
          "SMS": "33689965433",
          "WHATSAPP": "33689965433"
        },
        "email": "ndicky0@ocn.ne.jp"
      }
    ],
    "listIds": [
      76
    ],
    "consentGroupIds": [
      1
    ],
    "newList": {
      "folderId": 2,
      "listName": "ContactImport - 2017-05"
    },
    "notifyUrl": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1",
    "smsBlacklist": false,
    "updateExistingContacts": true
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/import`

It returns the background process ID which on completion calls the notify URL that you have set in the input. **Note**: - Any contact attribute that doesn't exist in your account will be ignored at import end.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "disableNotification": false,
  "emailBlacklist": false,
  "emptyContactsAttributes": true,
  "fileBody": "NAME;SURNAME;EMAIL\nSmith;John;john.smith@example.com\nRoger;Ellie;ellie36@example.com",
  "fileUrl": "https://importfile.domain.com",
  "jsonBody": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "BIRTHDAY": "11/02/1989",
        "COUNTRY": "DE",
        "FNAME": "Dicky",
        "LANDLINE_NUMBER": "33689965433",
        "LNAME": "Noemi",
        "PREFERED_COLOR": "BLACK",
        "SMS": "33689965433",
        "WHATSAPP": "33689965433"
      },
      "email": "ndicky0@ocn.ne.jp"
    }
  ],
  "listIds": [
    76
  ],
  "consentGroupIds": [
    1
  ],
  "newList": {
    "folderId": 2,
    "listName": "ContactImport - 2017-05"
  },
  "notifyUrl": "http://requestb.in/173lyyx1",
  "smsBlacklist": false,
  "updateExistingContacts": true
}
```

<h3 id="import-contacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to import contacts in Brevo. To know more about the expected format, please have a look at ``https://help.brevo.com/hc/en-us/articles/209499265-Build-contacts-lists-for-your-email-marketing-campaigns``|
|» disableNotification|body|boolean|false|To disable email notification|
|» emailBlacklist|body|boolean|false|To blacklist all the contacts for email|
|» emptyContactsAttributes|body|boolean|false|To facilitate the choice to erase any attribute of the existing contacts with empty value. emptyContactsAttributes = true means the empty fields in your import will erase any attribute that currently contain data in Brevo, & emptyContactsAttributes = false means the empty fields will not affect your existing data ( **only available if `updateExistingContacts` set to true **)<br>|
|» fileBody|body|string|false|**Mandatory if fileUrl and jsonBody is not defined.** CSV content to be imported. Use semicolon to separate multiple attributes. **Maximum allowed file body size is 10MB** . However we recommend a safe limit of around 8 MB to avoid the issues caused due to increase of file body size while parsing. Please use fileUrl instead to import bigger files.<br>|
|» fileUrl|body|string(url)|false|**Mandatory if fileBody and jsonBody is not defined.** URL of the file to be imported (**no local file**). Possible file formats: #### .txt, .csv, .json<br>|
|» jsonBody|body|[object]|false|**Mandatory if fileUrl and fileBody is not defined.** JSON content to be imported. **Maximum allowed json body size is 10MB** . However we recommend a safe limit of around 8 MB to avoid the issues caused due to increase of json body size while parsing. Please use fileUrl instead to import bigger files.<br>|
|» » attributes|body|object|false|List of attributes to be imported|
|» » email|body|string|false|none|
|» listIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|**Mandatory if newList is not defined.** Ids of the lists in which the contacts shall be imported. For example, **[2, 4, 7]**.<br>|
|» consentGroupIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|**Optional.** Ids of the consent groups to which all imported contacts will be added. Requires consent groups to be enabled for the organisation. For example, **[1, 3]**.<br>|
|» newList|body|object|false|To create a new list and import the contacts into it, pass the listName and an optional folderId.|
|» » folderId|body|integer(int64)|false|Id of the folder where this new list shall be created. **Mandatory if listName is not empty**<br>|
|» » listName|body|string|false|List with listName will be created first and users will be imported in it. **Mandatory if listIds is empty**.<br>|
|» notifyUrl|body|string(url)|false|URL that will be called once the import process is finished. For reference, https://help.brevo.com/hc/en-us/articles/360007666479|
|» smsBlacklist|body|boolean|false|To blacklist all the contacts for sms|
|» updateExistingContacts|body|boolean|false|To facilitate the choice to update the existing contacts|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "processId": 78
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

## Create a list

<a id="opIdcreateList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/lists \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "folderId": 2,
    "name": "Magento Customer - ES"
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/lists`

Create a new contact list inside a specified folder. Both the list name and the parent folder ID are required. The newly created list will be empty and ready to receive contacts via the add contacts endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "folderId": 2,
  "name": "Magento Customer - ES"
}
```

|body|body|object|true|Values to create a list|
|» folderId|body|integer(int64)|true|Id of the parent folder in which this list is to be created|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the list|

## Get a list's details

<a id="opIdgetList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/lists/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /contacts/lists/{listId}`

Retrieve the details of a specific contact list by its ID, including its name, folder ID, creation date, subscriber counts, and campaign statistics. You can optionally filter campaign statistics by providing startDate and endDate parameters (both must be used together in YYYY-MM-DD format).

<h3 id="get-a-lists-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|listId|path|integer(int64)|true|Id of the list|
|startDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if endDate is used**. Starting (urlencoded) UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to aggregate the sent email campaigns for a specific list id. **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result**<br>|
|endDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if startDate is used**. Ending (urlencoded) UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to aggregate the sent email campaigns for a specific list id. **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result**<br>|

## Update a list

<a id="opIdupdateList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/lists/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "folderId": 2,
    "name": "Magento Customer - ES"
  }'
```

`PUT /contacts/lists/{listId}`

Update an existing contact list identified by its ID. You can update the list name, move it to a different folder by providing a new folderId, or both. Only one of the two parameters (name, folderId) needs to be provided per request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "folderId": 2,
  "name": "Magento Customer - ES"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|listId|path|integer(int64)|true|Id of the list|
|body|body|object|true|Values to update a list|
|» folderId|body|integer(int64)|false|Id of the folder in which the list is to be moved. Either of the two parameters (name, folderId) can be updated at a time.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the list. Either of the two parameters (name, folderId) can be updated at a time.|

## Get contacts in a list

<a id="opIdgetContactsFromList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/lists/0/contacts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /contacts/lists/{listId}/contacts`

Retrieve all contacts belonging to a specific list, identified by its list ID. Results are paginated with a default of 50 contacts per page (maximum 500) and sorted in descending order of creation. You can optionally filter contacts by their modification date using the modifiedSince parameter.

<h3 id="get-contacts-in-a-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|listId|path|integer(int64)|true|Id of the list|
|modifiedSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the contacts modified after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.**<br>|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document of the page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

## Add existing contacts to a list

<a id="opIdaddContactToList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/lists/0/contacts/add \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "emails": [
      "jeff32@example.com",
      "jim56@example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "emails": [
    "jeff32@example.com",
    "jim56@example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-existing-contacts-to-a-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|listId|path|integer(int64)|true|Id of the list|
|body|body|object|true|Emails addresses OR IDs OR EXT_ID attributes of the contacts|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» emails|body|[string(email)]|false|Emails to add to a list. You can pass a **maximum of 150 emails** for addition in one request. **_If you need to add the emails in bulk, please prefer /contacts/import api._**<br>|

|» ids|body|[integer(int64)]|false|IDs to add to a list. You can pass a **maximum of 150 IDs** for addition in one request. **_If you need to add the emails in bulk, please prefer /contacts/import api._**<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» extIds|body|[string]|false|EXT_ID attributes to add to a list. You can pass a **maximum of 150 EXT_ID attributes** for addition in one request. **_If you need to add the emails in bulk, please prefer /contacts/import api._**<br>|

## Delete a contact from a list

<a id="opIdremoveContactFromList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/lists/0/contacts/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "all": true
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/lists/{listId}/contacts/remove`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "all": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-contact-from-a-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|listId|path|integer(int64)|true|Id of the list|
|body|body|object|true|Emails adresses OR IDs OR EXT_ID attributes of the contacts OR 'all' true|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» emails|body|[string(email)]|false|**Required if 'all' is false and 'ids', 'extIds' are empty.** Emails to remove from a list. You can pass a **maximum of 150 emails** for removal in one request.<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» ids|body|[integer(int64)]|false|**Required if 'all' is false and 'emails', 'extIds' are empty.** IDs to remove from a list. You can pass a **maximum of 150 IDs** for removal in one request.<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» all|body|boolean|false|**Required if 'emails', 'extIds' and 'ids' are empty.** Remove all existing contacts from a list. A process will be created in this scenario. You can fetch the process details to know about the progress<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» extIds|body|[string]|false|**Required if 'all' is false, 'ids' and 'emails' are empty.** EXT_ID attributes to remove from a list. You can pass a **maximum of 150 EXT_ID attributes** for removal in one request.<br>|

```json
  "processId": 5,
  "total": 23
}
```

## Get all the segments

<a id="opIdgetSegments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/segments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /contacts/segments`

Retrieve all contact segments defined in your Brevo account with support for pagination and sorting. Results default to 10 segments per page (maximum 50) sorted in descending order of creation. Each segment includes its ID, name, category name, and last update timestamp.

<h3 id="get-all-the-segments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document of the page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

## Get a contact's details

<a id="opIdgetContactInfo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /contacts/{identifier}`

<Note>Follow this format when passing a "SMS" phone number as an attribute.
Accepted Number Formats 91xxxxxxxxxx +91xxxxxxxxxx 0091xxxxxxxxxx</Note>
There are 2 ways to get a contact <br><br> Option 1- https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/{identifier} <br><br> Option 2- https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/{identifier}?identifierType={} <br> <br> Option 1 only works if identifierType is email_id (for EMAIL), phone_id (for SMS) or contact_id (for ID of the contact),where you can directly pass the value of EMAIL, SMS and ID of the contact.   <br><br> Option 2 works for all identifierType, use email_id for EMAIL attribute, phone_id for SMS attribute, contact_id for ID of the contact, ext_id for EXT_ID attribute, whatsapp_id for WHATSAPP attribute, landline_number_id for LANDLINE_NUMBER attribute <br><br>Along with the contact details, this endpoint will show the statistics of contact for the recent 90 days by default. To fetch the earlier statistics, please use Get contact campaign stats ``https://developers.brevo.com/reference/contacts-7#getcontactstats`` endpoint with the appropriate date ranges.

<h3 id="get-a-contacts-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|identifier|path|string \| integer|true|Email (urlencoded) OR ID of the contact OR its SMS attribute value OR EXT_ID attribute (urlencoded)|
|identifierType|query|string|false|email_id for Email, phone_id for SMS attribute, contact_id for ID of the contact, ext_id for EXT_ID attribute, whatsapp_id for WHATSAPP attribute, landline_number_id for LANDLINE_NUMBER attribute|
|startDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if endDate is used.** Starting date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the statistic events specific to campaigns. Must be lower than equal to endDate. Must not be greater than the current date.<br>|
|endDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if startDate is used.** Ending date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the statistic events specific to campaigns. Must be greater than equal to startDate. Must not be greater than the current date.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|identifierType|email_id|
|identifierType|phone_id|
|identifierType|contact_id|
|identifierType|ext_id|
|identifierType|whatsapp_id|
|identifierType|landline_number_id|

## Update a contact

<a id="opIdupdateContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "attributes": {
      "COUNTRIES": [
        "India",
        "China"
      ],
      "EMAIL": "newemail@domain.com",
      "FNAME": "Ellie",
      "LNAME": "Roger"
    },
    "emailBlacklisted": false,
    "ext_id": "updateExternalId",
    "listIds": [
      65
    ],
    "smsBlacklisted": true,
    "smtpBlacklistSender": [
      "user@example.com"
    ],
    "unlinkListIds": [
      36
    ],
    "forceMerge": true
  }'
```

`PUT /contacts/{identifier}`

<Note>Follow this format when passing a "SMS" phone number as an attribute.
Accepted Number Formats 91xxxxxxxxxx +91xxxxxxxxxx 0091xxxxxxxxxx</Note>
There are 2 ways to update a contact <br><br> Option 1- https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/{identifier} <br><br> Option 2- https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/{identifier}?identifierType={} <br> <br> Option 1 only works if identifierType is email_id (for EMAIL) or contact_id (for ID of the contact),where you can directly pass the value of EMAIL and ID of the contact.   <br><br> Option 2 works for all identifierType, use email_id for EMAIL attribute, contact_id for ID of the contact, ext_id for EXT_ID attribute, phone_id for SMS attribute, whatsapp_id for WHATSAPP attribute, landline_number_id for LANDLINE_NUMBER attribute

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "COUNTRIES": [
      "India",
      "China"
    ],
    "EMAIL": "newemail@domain.com",
    "FNAME": "Ellie",
    "LNAME": "Roger"
  },
  "emailBlacklisted": false,
  "ext_id": "updateExternalId",
  "listIds": [
    65
  ],
  "smsBlacklisted": true,
  "smtpBlacklistSender": [
    "user@example.com"
  ],
  "unlinkListIds": [
    36
  ],
  "forceMerge": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|identifier|path|string \| integer|true|Email (urlencoded) OR ID of the contact OR EXT_ID attribute (urlencoded) OR its SMS attribute value OR its WHATSAPP attribute value OR its LANDLINE_NUMBER attribute value|
|identifierType|query|string|false|email_id for Email, contact_id for ID of the contact, ext_id for EXT_ID attribute, phone_id for SMS attribute, whatsapp_id for WHATSAPP attribute, landline_number_id for LANDLINE_NUMBER attribute|
|body|body|object|true|Values to update a contact|
|» attributes|body|object|false|Pass the set of attributes to be updated. **These attributes must be present in your account**. To update existing email address of a contact with the new one please pass EMAIL in attributes. For example, **{ "EMAIL":"newemail@domain.com", "FNAME":"Ellie", "LNAME":"Roger", "COUNTRIES":["India","China"]}**. The attribute's parameter should be passed in capital letter while updating a contact. Values that don't match the attribute type (e.g. text or string in a date attribute) will be ignored .Keep in mind transactional attributes can be updated the same way as normal attributes. Mobile Number in **SMS** field should be passed with proper country code. For example: **{"SMS":"+91xxxxxxxxxx"} or {"SMS":"0091xxxxxxxxxx"}**<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|number \| string \| boolean \| [string]|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» emailBlacklisted|body|boolean|false|Set/unset this field to blacklist/allow the contact for emails (emailBlacklisted = true)|
|» ext_id|body|string|false|Pass your own Id to update ext_id of a contact.|
|» listIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Ids of the lists to add the contact to|
|» smsBlacklisted|body|boolean|false|Set/unset this field to blacklist/allow the contact for SMS (smsBlacklisted = true)|
|» smtpBlacklistSender|body|[string(email)]|false|transactional email forbidden sender for contact. Use only for email Contact|
|» unlinkListIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Ids of the lists to remove the contact from|
|» forceMerge|body|boolean|false|When true, if the contact being updated shares an identifier (email, SMS, ext_id, whatsapp, landline) with an existing contact, the two contacts are force-merged. The contact with the most recent `last_modified` timestamp is retained; the other is deleted. When false (default), a 4xx error is returned on identifier conflict.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|identifierType|email_id|
|identifierType|contact_id|
|identifierType|ext_id|
|identifierType|phone_id|
|identifierType|whatsapp_id|
|identifierType|landline_number_id|

```json
  "code": "duplicate_parameter",

    "duplicate_identifiers": [
      "email"
    ]
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "code": "duplicate_parameter",

    "duplicate_identifiers": [
      "email"

```

```json
{
  "code": "duplicate_parameter",
  "message": "email is already associated with another Contact",
  "metadata": {
    "duplicate_identifiers": [
      "email"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Get email campaigns' statistics for a contact

<a id="opIdgetContactStats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/string/campaignStats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /contacts/{identifier}/campaignStats`

Retrieve email campaign statistics for a specific contact identified by email address or numeric ID. Statistics include messages sent, opens, clicks, hard/soft bounces, deliveries, unsubscriptions, complaints, and transactional attributes. By default, data covers the last 90 days; use startDate and endDate parameters (YYYY-MM-DD) to specify a custom range with a maximum span of 90 days.

<h3 id="get-email-campaigns-statistics-for-a-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|identifier|path|string \| integer|true|Email (urlencoded) OR ID of the contact|
|startDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if endDate is used.** Starting date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the statistic events specific to campaigns. Must be lower than equal to endDate. Must not be greater than the current date.<br>|
|endDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if startDate is used.** Ending date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the statistic events specific to campaigns. Must be greater than equal to startDate. Must not be greater than the current date. Maximum difference between startDate and endDate should not be greater than 90 days.<br>|

## Create a consent group

<a id="opIdcreateConsentGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/consent-groups \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Newsletter EU",
    "description": "Consent group for EU newsletter subscribers",
    "signupMode": "manual",
    "listIds": [
      0
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/consent-groups`

Creates a new consent group for the account.

<Note>This endpoint is only available when the Consent Groups feature is enabled for your account.</Note>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Newsletter EU",
  "description": "Consent group for EU newsletter subscribers",
  "signupMode": "manual",
  "listIds": [
    0
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-consent-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateConsentGroupRequest](#schemacreateconsentgrouprequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Unique name for the consent group (max 255 characters)|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional description (max 500 characters)|
|» signupMode|body|string|true|Controls how contacts are added to the group. `manual` — contacts are added explicitly via the API. `automatic` — contacts are added automatically at signup.|
|» listIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Optional list of contact list IDs. Contacts from these lists will be copied once into this consent group at creation time.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» signupMode|manual|
|» signupMode|automatic|

Possible error codes: `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` (name or signupMode missing), `INVALID_SIGNUP_MODE` (invalid signupMode value), `FIELD_TOO_LONG` (name exceeds 255 or description exceeds 500 characters), `INVALID_LIST_ID` (one or more listIds are invalid).|[errorModel](#schemaerrormodel)|

<h1 id="brevo-api-conversations">Conversations</h1>

## Sets agent's status to online for 2-3 minutes

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/conversations/agentOnlinePing \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "agentId": "d9nKoegKSjmCtyK78"
  }'
```

`POST /conversations/agentOnlinePing`

Sets the agent's status to online for 2-3 minutes. We recommend pinging this endpoint every minute for as long as the agent has to be considered online. You must provide either `agentId` alone, or all three of `agentEmail` + `agentName` + `receivedFrom`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "agentId": "d9nKoegKSjmCtyK78"
}
```

<h3 id="sets-agents-status-to-online-for-2-3-minutes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» agentEmail|body|string(email)|false|Agent's email address. When sending online pings from a standalone system, it's hard to maintain a 1-to-1 relationship between the users of both systems. In this case, an agent can be specified by their email address. If there's no agent with the specified email address in your Brevo organization, a dummy agent will be created automatically.|
|» agentId|body|string|false|Agent ID. It can be found on the agent's page or received <a href="https://developers.brevo.com/docs/conversations-webhooks">from a webhook</a>. Alternatively, you can use `agentEmail` + `agentName` + `receivedFrom` instead (all 3 fields required).|
|» agentName|body|string|false|Agent's name.|
|» receivedFrom|body|string|false|Mark your messages to distinguish messages created by you from the others.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<h3 id="sets-agents-status-to-online-for-2-3-minutes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

## Send a message as an agent

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/conversations/messages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "agentId": "d9nKoegKSjmCtyK78",
    "text": "Hello! How can I help you?",
    "visitorId": "kZMvWhf8npAu3H6qd57w2Hv6nh6rnxvg"
  }'
```

`POST /conversations/messages`

Send a message as an agent to an existing visitor's conversation. You must provide either `agentId` alone, or all three of `agentEmail` + `agentName` + `receivedFrom` to identify the agent.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "agentId": "d9nKoegKSjmCtyK78",
  "text": "Hello! How can I help you?",
  "visitorId": "kZMvWhf8npAu3H6qd57w2Hv6nh6rnxvg"
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-message-as-an-agent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» agentEmail|body|string(email)|false|Agent's email address. When sending messages from a standalone system, it's hard to maintain a 1-to-1 relationship between the users of both systems. In this case, an agent can be specified by their email address.|
|» agentId|body|string|false|Agent ID. It can be found on the agent's page or received <a href="https://developers.brevo.com/docs/conversations-webhooks">from a webhook</a>. Alternatively, you can use `agentEmail` + `agentName` + `receivedFrom` instead (all 3 fields required).|
|» agentName|body|string|false|Agent's name.|
|» receivedFrom|body|string|false|Mark your messages to distinguish messages created by you from the others.|
|» text|body|string|true|Message text.|
|» visitorId|body|string|true|Visitor's ID received <a href="https://developers.brevo.com/docs/conversations-webhooks">from a webhook</a> or generated by you to <a href="https://developers.brevo.com/docs/customize-the-widget#identifying-existing-users">bind an existing user account to Conversations</a>.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "agentId": "d9nKoegKSjmCtyK78",
  "createdAt": 1482512803740,
  "html": "Hello! How can I help you?",
  "id": "eYBEm3gq3zc5ayE2g",
  "isMissed": false,
  "isMissedByVisitor": false,
  "isPushed": false,
  "isTrigger": false,
  "receivedFrom": "SuperAwesomeHelpdesk",
  "text": "Hello! How can I help you?",
  "type": "agent",
  "visitorId": "kZMvWhf8npAu3H6qd57w2Hv6nh6rnxvg"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-message-as-an-agent-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Newly created message is returned as a response.|[ConversationsMessage](#schemaconversationsmessage)|
|400|Bad Request|bad request|Inline|

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /conversations/pushedMessages`

Send an automated (pushed) message to a visitor on behalf of an agent. Example use cases: order status updates, announcing new features in your web app, etc.

> Body parameter


<h1 id="brevo-api-ecommerce">Ecommerce</h1>

## Return all your categories

<a id="opIdgetCategories"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/categories \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /categories`

Retrieve a paginated list of all ecommerce categories stored in your Brevo account. Results are sorted by creation date in descending order by default, and can be filtered by category IDs, name, modification date, creation date, or deletion status. The response includes a `count` field with the total number of matching categories, and pagination defaults to 50 categories per page (maximum 100).

<h3 id="return-all-your-categories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document in the page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|
|ids|query|[string]|false|Filter by category ids|
|name|query|string|false|Filter by category name|
|modifiedSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the categories modified after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.**<br>|
|createdSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the categories created after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.**<br>|
|isDeleted|query|string|false|Filter categories by their deletion status. If `false` is passed, only categories that are not deleted will be returned.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "categories": [
    {
      "createdAt": "2021-12-31T11:42:35.638Z",
      "id": "C19",
      "isDeleted": true,
      "modifiedAt": "2022-03-03T14:48:31.867Z",
      "name": "Food",
      "url": "http://mydomain.com/category/food"
    },
    {
      "createdAt": "2021-12-31T11:42:35.638Z",
      "id": "C20",
      "isDeleted": true,
      "modifiedAt": "2022-03-03T14:48:31.867Z",
      "name": "clothing",
      "url": "http://mydomain.com/category/clothing"
    }
  ],
  "count": 2
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<h3 id="return-all-your-categories-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|400|Bad Request|bad request|Inline|

## Create/Update a category

<a id="opIdcreateUpdateCategory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/categories \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "deletedAt": "2017-05-12T12:30:00Z",
    "id": "CAT123",
    "isDeleted": true,
    "name": "Electronics",
    "updateEnabled": false,
    "url": "http://mydomain.com/category/electronics"
  }'
```

`POST /categories`

Create a new ecommerce category or update an existing one, identified by the mandatory `id` field. When `updateEnabled` is set to `false` (the default), the endpoint performs an insert and returns `201`; if the category ID already exists, a `400` error is returned. When `updateEnabled` is `true`, the endpoint performs an upsert, returning `201` for a new category or `204` when an existing category is updated. The `name` field is mandatory for creation but optional for updates.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "deletedAt": "2017-05-12T12:30:00Z",
  "id": "CAT123",
  "isDeleted": true,
  "name": "Electronics",
  "updateEnabled": false,
  "url": "http://mydomain.com/category/electronics"
}
```

<h3 id="createupdate-a-category-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to create/update a category|
|» deletedAt|body|string|false|UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) of the category deleted from the shop's database|
|» id|body|string|true|Unique Category ID as saved in the shop<br>|
|» isDeleted|body|boolean|false|category deleted from the shop's database|
|» name|body|string|false|**Mandatory in case of creation**. Name of the Category, as displayed in the shop<br>|
|» updateEnabled|body|boolean|false|Facilitate to update the existing category in the same request (updateEnabled = true)|
|» url|body|string|false|URL to the category|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 21
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<h3 id="createupdate-a-category-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Category created|Inline|
|204|No Content|Category updated|None|
|400|Bad Request|bad request|Inline|

## Create categories in batch

<a id="opIdcreateUpdateBatchCategory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/categories/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "categories": [
      {
        "deletedAt": "2017-05-12T12:30:00Z",
        "id": "CAT123",
        "isDeleted": true,
        "name": "Electronics",
        "url": "http://mydomain.com/category/electronics"
      }
    ],
    "updateEnabled": true
  }'
```

`POST /categories/batch`

Create or update multiple ecommerce categories in a single request. The `categories` array accepts up to 100 category objects, each requiring a unique `id`. When `updateEnabled` is `false` (the default), all categories are inserted as new; if any ID already exists, a `400` error is returned. When `updateEnabled` is `true`, existing categories are updated and new ones are created via upsert. Duplicate IDs within the same request payload are rejected. The response returns the count of created and updated categories.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "categories": [
    {
      "deletedAt": "2017-05-12T12:30:00Z",
      "id": "CAT123",
      "isDeleted": true,
      "name": "Electronics",
      "url": "http://mydomain.com/category/electronics"
    }
  ],
  "updateEnabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-categories-in-batch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to create a batch of categories|
|» categories|body|[object]|true|array of categories objects|
|» » deletedAt|body|string|false|UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) of the category deleted from the shop's database|
|» » id|body|string|true|Unique Category ID as saved in the shop<br>|
|» » isDeleted|body|boolean|false|category deleted from the shop's database|
|» » name|body|string|false|**Mandatory in case of creation**. Name of the Category, as displayed in the shop<br>|
|» » url|body|string|false|URL to the category|
|» updateEnabled|body|boolean|false|Facilitate to update the existing categories in the same request (updateEnabled = true)|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "createdCount": 2,
  "updatedCount": 7
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<h3 id="create-categories-in-batch-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Category created and updated|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|bad request|Inline|

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

## Get attribution metrics for one or more Brevo campaigns or workflows

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/ecommerce/attribution/metrics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /ecommerce/attribution/metrics`

Retrieve aggregated ecommerce attribution metrics for one or more Brevo email campaigns, SMS campaigns, or automation workflows. You can optionally filter by a date range using `periodFrom` and `periodTo` in RFC3339 format. The response includes per-source metrics (orders count, revenue, and average basket) as well as aggregated totals across all requested sources.

<h3 id="get-attribution-metrics-for-one-or-more-brevo-campaigns-or-workflows-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|periodFrom|query|string(date-time)|false|When getting metrics for a specific period, define the starting datetime in RFC3339 format|
|periodTo|query|string(date-time)|false|When getting metrics for a specific period, define the end datetime in RFC3339 format|
|emailCampaignId[]|query|[string]|false|The email campaign ID(s) to get metrics for|
|smsCampaignId[]|query|[string]|false|The SMS campaign ID(s) to get metrics for|
|automationWorkflowEmailId[]|query|[string]|false|The automation workflow ID(s) to get email attribution metrics for|
|automationWorkflowSmsId[]|query|[string]|false|The automation workflow ID(s) to get SMS attribution metrics for|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "averageBasket": 3,
      "conversionSource": "email_campaign",
      "id": "sale01",
      "ordersCount": 300,
      "revenue": 900
    },
    {
      "averageBasket": 4,
      "conversionSource": "email_campaign",
      "id": "sale02",
      "ordersCount": 200,
      "revenue": 800
    }
  ],
  "totals": {
    "averageBasket": 3.4,
    "ordersCount": 500,
    "revenue": 1700
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

`GET /ecommerce/attribution/products/{conversionSource}/{conversionSourceId}`

Each product entry includes its ID, name, SKU, image URL, product URL, price, revenue, and orders count.   -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
```bash
  -d '{
    "code": "EUR"
  }'
```

`POST /ecommerce/config/displayCurrency`

Set or update the ISO 4217 display currency code for your Brevo ecommerce account. This currency determines how monetary values are displayed in the ecommerce dashboard and reports. The provided currency code must be a valid ISO 4217 code; invalid codes result in a `422` error. Returns a `403` error if ecommerce is not activated on the account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "code": "EUR"
}
```

|createdSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the orders created after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.**<br>|

## Return all your products

<a id="opIdgetProducts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/products \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /products`

Retrieve a paginated list of all ecommerce products stored in your Brevo account. Results are sorted by creation date in descending order by default, and can be filtered by product IDs, name (minimum 3 characters), price range, category IDs, modification date, creation date, or deletion status. Use the `search` parameter to query across SKU, name, and ID simultaneously — results are prioritized as exact SKU match > SKU prefix match > name match > ID match. Pagination defaults to 50 products per page (maximum 1000), and the response includes a `count` field with the total number of matching products.

<h3 id="return-all-your-products-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document in the page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|
|ids|query|[string]|false|Filter by product ids|
|search|query|string|false|Search products simultaneously across SKU, name, and ID fields. Results are returned in the following priority order: **exact SKU match** > **SKU prefix match** > **name match** > **ID match**. For example, `?search=123` on products with `{sku: "123"}` and `{sku: "123456"}` returns the exact SKU match first.|
|name|query|string|false|Filter by product name, minimum 3 characters should be present for search.|
|price[lte]|query|number|false|Price filter for products less than and equals to particular amount|
|price[gte]|query|number|false|Price filter for products greater than and equals to particular amount|
|price[lt]|query|number|false|Price filter for products less than particular amount|
|price[gt]|query|number|false|Price filter for products greater than particular amount|
|price[eq]|query|number|false|Price filter for products equals to particular amount|
|price[ne]|query|number|false|Price filter for products not equals to particular amount|
|alternativePrice[lte]|query|number|false|Alternative price filter for products less than and equals to particular amount|
|alternativePrice[gte]|query|number|false|Alternative price filter for products greater than and equals to particular amount|
|alternativePrice[lt]|query|number|false|Alternative price filter for products less than particular amount|
|alternativePrice[gt]|query|number|false|Alternative price filter for products greater than particular amount|
|alternativePrice[eq]|query|number|false|Alternative price filter for products equals to particular amount|
|alternativePrice[ne]|query|number|false|Alternative price filter for products not equals to particular amount|
|categories|query|[string]|false|Filter by categories ids|
|modifiedSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the products modified after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.**<br>|
|createdSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the products created after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.**<br>|
|sortByField|query|string|false|Sort the results by a specific field. Default sort field is `created_at` when not passed.<br>|
|isDeleted|query|string|false|Filter products by their deletion status. If `false` is passed, only products that are not deleted will be returned.<br>|

|sort|desc|

## Create/Update a product

<a id="opIdcreateUpdateProduct"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/products \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "brand": "Adidas",
    "categories": [
      "string"
    ],
    "deletedAt": "2017-05-12T12:30:00Z",
    "description": "Shoes for sports",
    "id": "P11",
    "imageUrl": "http://mydomain.com/product-absoulte-url/img.jpeg",
    "isDeleted": true,
    "metaInfo": {
      "brand": "addidas",
      "description": "Shoes for sports"
    },
    "name": "Iphone 11",
    "parentId": "string",
    "price": 0,
    "alternativePrice": 0,
    "sku": "string",
    "stock": 100,
    "updateEnabled": false,
    "url": "http://mydomain.com/product/electronics/product1"
  }'
```

`POST /products`

Create a new ecommerce product or update an existing one, identified by the mandatory `id` field. When `updateEnabled` is `false` (the default), the endpoint inserts a new product and returns `201`; if the product ID already exists, a `400` error is returned. When `updateEnabled` is `true`, the endpoint performs an upsert, returning `201` for a new product or `204` for an update. The `name` field is mandatory for creation but optional for updates. Product images are downloaded, validated (max 5 MB, formats: jpeg, jpg, png, bmp, gif, webp), and re-hosted on S3. The `metaInfo` object supports up to 20 keys with a cumulative size limit of approximately 1000 KB.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "brand": "Adidas",
  "categories": [
    "string"
  ],
  "deletedAt": "2017-05-12T12:30:00Z",
  "description": "Shoes for sports",
  "id": "P11",
  "imageUrl": "http://mydomain.com/product-absoulte-url/img.jpeg",
  "isDeleted": true,
  "metaInfo": {
    "brand": "addidas",
    "description": "Shoes for sports"
  },
  "name": "Iphone 11",
  "parentId": "string",
  "price": 0,
  "alternativePrice": 0,
  "sku": "string",
  "stock": 100,
  "updateEnabled": false,
  "url": "http://mydomain.com/product/electronics/product1"
}
```

<h3 id="createupdate-a-product-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to create/update a product|
|» brand|body|string|false|Brand of the product|
|» categories|body|[string]|false|Category ID-s of the product|
|» deletedAt|body|string|false|UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) of the product deleted from the shop's database|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the product|
|» id|body|string(string)|true|Product ID for which you requested the details|
|» imageUrl|body|string(string)|false|Absolute URL to the cover image of the product|
|» isDeleted|body|boolean|false|product deleted from the shop's database|
|» metaInfo|body|object|false|Meta data of product such as description, vendor, producer, stock level. The total characters of cumulative metaInfo shall not exceed **20000 characters**.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string \| integer|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|**Mandatory in case of creation**. Name of the product, as displayed in the shop|
|» parentId|body|string(string)|false|Parent product id of the product|
|» price|body|number(float)|false|Price of the product|
|» alternativePrice|body|number(float)|false|Alternative price of the product|
|» sku|body|string(string)|false|Product identifier from the shop|
|» stock|body|number|false|Current stock value of the product from the shop's database|
|» updateEnabled|body|boolean|false|Facilitate to update the existing product in the same request (updateEnabled = true)|
|» url|body|string(string)|false|URL to the product|

```json
  "id": 21
}
```

```json
}
```

## Create products in batch

<a id="opIdcreateUpdateBatchProducts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/products/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "products": [
      {
        "brand": "Adidas",
        "categories": [
          "string"
        ],
        "deletedAt": "2017-05-12T12:30:00Z",
        "description": "Shoes for sports",
        "id": "P11",
        "imageUrl": "http://mydomain.com/product-absoulte-url/img.jpeg",
        "isDeleted": true,
        "metaInfo": {
          "brand": "addidas",
          "description": "Shoes for sports"
        },
        "name": "Iphone 11",
        "parentId": "string",
        "price": 0,
        "alternativePrice": 0,
        "sku": "string",
        "stock": 100,
        "url": "http://mydomain.com/product/electronics/product1"
      }
    ],
    "updateEnabled": true
  }'
```

`POST /products/batch`

Create or update multiple ecommerce products in a single request. The `products` array accepts up to 100 product objects for creation (or up to 1000 when `updateEnabled` is `true` and the account has an increased limit). Each product requires a unique `id` and `name` (name is mandatory for creation only). When `updateEnabled` is `false`, all products are inserted as new; if any ID already exists, a `400` error is returned. When `updateEnabled` is `true`, existing products are updated and new ones are created via upsert. Duplicate IDs within the same request payload are rejected. The response returns the count of created and updated products.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "products": [
    {
      "brand": "Adidas",
      "categories": [
        "string"
      ],
      "deletedAt": "2017-05-12T12:30:00Z",
      "description": "Shoes for sports",
      "id": "P11",
      "imageUrl": "http://mydomain.com/product-absoulte-url/img.jpeg",
      "isDeleted": true,
      "metaInfo": {
        "brand": "addidas",
        "description": "Shoes for sports"
      },
      "name": "Iphone 11",
      "parentId": "string",
      "price": 0,
      "alternativePrice": 0,
      "sku": "string",
      "stock": 100,
      "url": "http://mydomain.com/product/electronics/product1"
    }
  ],
  "updateEnabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-products-in-batch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to create a batch of products|
|» products|body|[object]|true|array of products objects|
|» » brand|body|string|false|Brand of the product|
|» » categories|body|[string]|false|Category ID-s of the product|
|» » deletedAt|body|string|false|UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) of the product deleted from the shop's database|
|» » description|body|string|false|Description of the product|
|» » id|body|string(string)|true|Product ID for which you requested the details|
|» » imageUrl|body|string(string)|false|Absolute URL to the cover image of the product|
|» » isDeleted|body|boolean|false|product deleted from the shop's database|
|» » metaInfo|body|object|false|Meta data of product such as description, vendor, producer, stock level. The total characters of cumulative metaInfo shall not exceed **20000 characters**.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string \| integer|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|**Mandatory in case of creation**. Name of the product, as displayed in the shop|
|» » parentId|body|string(string)|false|Parent product id of the product|
|» » price|body|number(float)|false|Price of the product|
|» » alternativePrice|body|number(float)|false|Alternative price of the product|
|» » sku|body|string(string)|false|Product identifier from the shop|
|» » stock|body|number|false|Current stock value of the product from the shop's database|
|» » url|body|string(string)|false|URL to the product|
|» updateEnabled|body|boolean|false|Facilitate to update the existing products in the same request (updateEnabled = true)|


`GET /products/{id}`

Retrieve the full details of a single ecommerce product by its unique ID. The response includes the product name, price, SKU, URL, image URLs (original and thumbnails), categories, stock level, meta information, creation and modification timestamps, and deletion status. ## Create a product alert for a contact

<a id="opIdcreateProductAlert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/products/string/alerts/back_in_stock \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "contactIdentifiers": {
      "email": "elly@example.com",
      "ext_id": "ExternalId",
      "sms": "+91xxxxxxxxxx"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /products/{id}/alerts/{type}`

Register a contact to receive an alert for a specific product event, such as `back_in_stock`. At least one contact identifier (`ext_id`, `email`, or `sms`) must be provided; when multiple are given, priority is `ext_id` > `email` > `sms`. Returns a `404` error if the product ID does not exist, and a `403` error if product alerts are not enabled for the account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "contactIdentifiers": {
    "email": "elly@example.com",
    "ext_id": "ExternalId",
    "sms": "+91xxxxxxxxxx"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-product-alert-for-a-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Product ID|
|type|path|string|true|Alert type|
|body|body|object|true|Contact identifier to associate the alert with (at least one is required). Priority is given to `ext_id` > `email` > `sms`|
|» contactIdentifiers|body|object|false|none|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|Email address of the contact|
|» » ext_id|body|string|false|Contact ID in your system|
|» » sms|body|string|false|Sms of the contact|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|back_in_stock|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

|400|Bad Request|Product alert could not be created|[errorModel](#schemaerrormodel)|

|403|Forbidden|Product alerts is not allowed for this account|[errorModel](#schemaerrormodel)|
|404|Not Found|Product ID not found|[errorModel](#schemaerrormodel)|

## Get all your coupon collections

<a id="opIdgetCouponCollections"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/couponCollections \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /couponCollections`

Retrieve a paginated list of all coupon collections in your Brevo account. Results can be sorted by creation date, remaining coupons count, or expiration date, in ascending or descending order. Pagination defaults to 50 collections per page (maximum 100).

<h3 id="get-all-your-coupon-collections-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents returned per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document on the page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results by creation time in ascending/descending order|
|sortBy|query|string|false|The field used to sort coupon collections|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|
|sortBy|createdAt|
|sortBy|remainingCoupons|
|sortBy|expirationDate|

## Create а coupon collection

<a id="opIdcreateCouponCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/couponCollections \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultCoupon": "Winter",
    "expirationDate": "2022-01-02T00:00:00Z",
    "name": "10%OFF",
    "remainingCouponsAlert": 5,
    "remainingDaysAlert": 5
  }'
```

`POST /couponCollections`

Create a new coupon collection with a name and a default coupon value. You can optionally set an expiration date in RFC3339 format and configure alert thresholds to receive email notifications when remaining coupons or remaining days before expiration fall below a specified number. The collection ID is auto-generated as a UUID and returned in the response.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultCoupon": "Winter",
  "expirationDate": "2022-01-02T00:00:00Z",
  "name": "10%OFF",
  "remainingCouponsAlert": 5,
  "remainingDaysAlert": 5
}
```

<h3 id="create-а-coupon-collection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to create a coupon collection|
|» defaultCoupon|body|string|true|Default coupons collection name|
|» expirationDate|body|string(date-time)|false|Specify an expiration date for the coupon collection in RFC3339 format. Use null to remove the expiration date.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the coupons collection|
|» remainingCouponsAlert|body|integer|false|Send a notification alert (email) when the remaining coupons count is equal or fall bellow this number. Use null to disable alerts.|
|» remainingDaysAlert|body|integer|false|Send a notification alert (email) when the remaining days until the expiration date are equal or fall bellow this number. Use null to disable alerts.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "23befbae-1505-47a8-bd27-e30ef739f32c"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```
