<h1 id="brevo-api-whatsapp-campaigns">WhatsApp Campaigns</h1>

## Return all your created WhatsApp campaigns

<a id="opIdgetWhatsAppCampaigns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/whatsappCampaigns \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /whatsappCampaigns`

Retrieve a paginated list of all your WhatsApp campaigns with their statistics and metadata. Results can be filtered by creation date range using startDate and endDate, with a default limit of 50 and maximum of 100 per page. The sort order defaults to descending by modification date.

<h3 id="return-all-your-created-whatsapp-campaigns-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if endDate is used**. Starting (urlencoded) UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to filter the WhatsApp campaigns created. **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result**<br>|
|endDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if startDate is used**. Ending (urlencoded) UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to filter the WhatsApp campaigns created. **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result**<br>|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document in the page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record modification. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "campaigns": [
    {
      "campaignName": "campaign_22",
      "campaignStatus": "sent",
      "createdAt": "2017-05-01T12:30:00Z",
      "errorReason": "NONE",
      "id": 1672035851100690,
      "invalidatedContacts": 0,
      "modifiedAt": "2017-05-01T12:30:00Z",
      "readPercentage": 28.57,
      "scheduledAt": "2022-12-27T09:50:00Z",
      "stats": {
        "delivered": 3,
        "notSent": 4,
        "read": 2,
        "sent": 3,
        "unsubscribe": 0
      },
      "templateId": 637660278078655
    }
  ],
  "count": 23
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<h3 id="return-all-your-created-whatsapp-campaigns-responses">Responses</h3>

|400|Bad Request|bad request|Inline|

## Create and Send a WhatsApp campaign

<a id="opIdcreateWhatsAppCampaign"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/whatsappCampaigns \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Test Campaign",
    "recipients": {
      "excludedListIds": [
        8
      ],
      "listIds": [
        32
      ],
      "segments": [
        23
      ]
    },
    "scheduledAt": "2017-06-01T12:30:00+02:00",
    "templateId": 19
  }'
```

`POST /whatsappCampaigns`

<Note>You can use this API for WhatsApp only if you have setup your WhatsApp account on Brevo platform. To setup your WhatsApp account, follow the steps in the guide below.
[Activating Whatsapp](https://developers.brevo.com/docs/whatsapp-campaigns-1) in your account</Note>
<Note>This API requires the List and Segment ids as recipients in Body params.You can use the below Contact endpoints to get the required information.
[Get all the Lists](https://developers.brevo.com/reference/getlists-1)
[Get all the Segments](https://developers.brevo.com/reference/getsegments)</Note>

```json
{
  "name": "Test Campaign",
  "recipients": {
    "excludedListIds": [
      8
    ],
    "listIds": [
      32
    ],

    ]
  },
  "scheduledAt": "2017-06-01T12:30:00+02:00",

}
```

## Return all your created WhatsApp templates

<a id="opIdgetWhatsAppTemplates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/whatsappCampaigns/template-list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /whatsappCampaigns/template-list`

Retrieve a paginated list of all your WhatsApp templates with their status, category, language, and metadata. Results can be filtered by creation date range and optionally by source (Automation or Conversations), with a default limit of 50 and maximum of 100 per page. The sort order defaults to descending by modification date.

<h3 id="return-all-your-created-whatsapp-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if endDate is used**. Starting (urlencoded) UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to filter the templates created. **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result**<br>|
|endDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if startDate is used**. Ending (urlencoded) UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to filter the templates created. **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result**<br>|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document in the page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record modification. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|
|source|query|string|false|source of the template|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|
|source|Automation|
|source|Conversations|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "templates": [
    {
      "category": "MARKETING",
      "createdAt": "2017-05-01T12:30:00Z",
      "errorReason": "NONE",
      "id": 235,
      "language": "en",
      "modifiedAt": "2017-05-01T12:30:00Z",
      "name": "campaign_22",
      "status": "approved",
      "type": "whatsapp"
    },
    {
      "category": "MARKETING",
      "createdAt": "2017-0",
      "errorReason": "NONE",
      "id": 124,
      "language": "",
      "modifiedAt": "2017-05-01T12:30:00Z",
      "name": "test-template",
      "status": "draft",
      "type": "whatsapp"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

## Update a WhatsApp campaign

<a id="opIdupdateWhatsAppCampaign"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/whatsappCampaigns/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "campaignName": "Test WhatsApp",
    "campaignStatus": "scheduled",
    "recipients": {
      "excludedListIds": [
        8
      ],
      "listIds": [
        32
      ],
      "segments": [
        23
      ]
    },
    "rescheduleFor": "2017-06-01T12:30:00+02:00"
  }'
```

`PUT /whatsappCampaigns/{campaignId}`

<Note>You can use this API for WhatsApp only if you have setup your WhatsApp account on Brevo platform. To setup your WhatsApp account, follow the steps in the guide below.
[Activating Whatsapp](https://developers.brevo.com/docs/whatsapp-campaigns-1) in your account</Note>
<Note>This API requires the List and Segment ids as recipients in Body params.You can use the below Contact endpoints to get the required information.
[Get all the Lists](https://developers.brevo.com/reference/getlists-1)
[Get all the Segments](https://developers.brevo.com/reference/getsegments)</Note>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "campaignName": "Test WhatsApp",
  "campaignStatus": "scheduled",
  "recipients": {
    "excludedListIds": [
      8
    ],
    "listIds": [
      32
    ],
    "segments": [
      23
    ]
  },
  "rescheduleFor": "2017-06-01T12:30:00+02:00"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-whatsapp-campaign-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|campaignId|path|integer(int64)|true|id of the campaign|
|body|body|object|true|Values to update a WhatsApp Campaign|
|» campaignName|body|string|false|Name of the campaign|
|» campaignStatus|body|string|false|Status of the campaign|
|» recipients|body|object|false|Segment ids and List ids to include/exclude from campaign|
|» » excludedListIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|List ids to exclude from the campaign|
|» » listIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|**Mandatory if scheduledAt is not empty**. List Ids to send the campaign to<br>|
|» » segments|body|[integer(int64)]|false|**Mandatory if listIds are not used**. Segment ids to send the campaign to.<br>|
|» rescheduleFor|body|string|false|Reschedule the sending UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) of campaign. **Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.For example: **2017-06-01T12:30:00+02:00** Use this field to update the scheduledAt of any existing draft or scheduled WhatsApp campaign.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» campaignStatus|scheduled|
|» campaignStatus|suspended|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<h1 id="brevo-api-companies">Companies</h1>

## Get all Companies

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/companies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /companies`

Retrieve a paginated list of companies with optional filtering, sorting, and search capabilities. Results are sorted by creation date in descending order by default, and can be filtered by attributes, linked contacts, linked deals, or modification/creation timestamps.

<h3 id="get-all-companies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filters[attributes.name]|query|string|false|Filter by attributes. If you have a filter for the owner on your side please send it as filters[attributes.owner] and utilize the account email for the filtering.|
|linkedContactsIds|query|integer(int64)|false|Filter by linked contacts ids|
|linkedDealsIds|query|string(objectID)|false|Filter by linked Deals ids|
|modifiedSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the companies modified after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.|
|createdSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the companies created after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document of the page|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order. Default order is **descending** by creation if `sort` is not passed|
|sortBy|query|string|false|The field used to sort field names.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

    {
      "attributes": {
        "created_at": "2022-01-13T19:04:24.376+05:30",

}
```

## Create a company

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/companies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "attributes": {
      "domain": "https://example.com",
      "industry": "Fabric",
      "owner": "60e68d60582a3b006f524197"
    },
    "countryCode": 91,
    "linkedContactsIds": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ],
    "linkedDealsIds": [
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
    ],
    "name": "company"
  }'
```

`POST /companies`

Create a new CRM company with the specified name, attributes, and optional associations to contacts and deals. The company name is required, and you can optionally provide a country code when a phone number attribute is included.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "domain": "https://example.com",
    "industry": "Fabric",
    "owner": "60e68d60582a3b006f524197"
  },
  "countryCode": 91,
  "linkedContactsIds": [
    1,
    2,
    3
  ],
  "linkedDealsIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
  ],
  "name": "company"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-company-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Company create data.|
|» attributes|body|object|false|Attributes for company creation|
|» countryCode|body|integer(int64)|false|Country code if phone_number is passed in attributes.|
|» linkedContactsIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Contact ids to be linked with company|
|» linkedDealsIds|body|[string(objectID)]|false|Deal ids to be linked with company|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of company|

`POST /companies/import`

Import companies from a CSV file with mapping options.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: false
mapping: {}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|» mapping|body|object|false|The mapping options in JSON format. Here is an example of the JSON structure: ```json {<br>  "link_entities": true, // Determines whether to link related entities during the import process<br>  "unlink_entities": false, // Determines whether to unlink related entities during the import process<br>  "update_existing_records": true, // Determines whether to update based on company ID or treat every row as create<br>  "unset_empty_attributes": false // Determines whether to unset a specific attribute during update if the values input is blank<br>} ```<br>|

```json
}
```

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/companies/string \
```

```bash
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

    "attributes": {

      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
    ],
    "name": "company"
  }'
```

`PATCH /companies/{id}`

Update an existing company''s attributes, name, linked contacts, or linked deals. Note that passing `linkedContactsIds` or `linkedDealsIds` replaces the entire list of associations, so omitted IDs will be removed. The company name cannot be set to an empty string.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "category": "label_2",
    "date": "2022-05-04T00:00:00+05:30",
    "domain": "xyz",
    "industry": "flipkart",
    "number_of_contacts": 1,
    "number_of_employees": 100,
    "owner": "5b1a17d914b73d35a76ca0c7",
    "phone_number": "81718441912",
    "revenue": 10000.34222
  },
  "countryCode": 91,
  "linkedContactsIds": [
    1,
    2,
    3
  ],
  "linkedDealsIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
  ],
  "name": "company"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|Updated company details.|
|» attributes|body|object|false|Attributes for company update|
|» countryCode|body|integer(int64)|false|Country code if phone_number is passed in attributes.|
|» linkedContactsIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Warning - Using PATCH on linkedContactIds replaces the list of linked contacts. Omitted IDs will be removed.|
|» linkedDealsIds|body|[string(objectID)]|false|Warning - Using PATCH on linkedDealsIds replaces the list of linked deals. Omitted IDs will be removed.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of company|

## Create a company/deal attribute

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/attributes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "attributeType": "single-select",
    "description": "This is a sample attribute description.",
    "label": "Attribute Label",
    "objectType": "companies",
    "optionsLabels": [
      "Option 1",
      "Option 2",
      "Option 3"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /crm/attributes`

Create a new custom attribute for companies or deals. The attribute label must be unique within the object type, cannot exceed 50 characters, and cannot use reserved names. For `single-select` or `multi-choice` attribute types, you must also provide the `optionsLabels` array.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attributeType": "single-select",
  "description": "This is a sample attribute description.",
  "label": "Attribute Label",
  "objectType": "companies",
  "optionsLabels": [
    "Option 1",
    "Option 2",
    "Option 3"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-companydeal-attribute-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Attribute creation data for a company/deal.|
|» attributeType|body|string|true|The type of attribute (must be one of the defined enums)|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the attribute|
|» label|body|string|true|The label for the attribute (max 50 characters, cannot be empty)|
|» objectType|body|string|true|The type of object the attribute belongs to. Must be either `companies` or `deals`.|
|» optionsLabels|body|[string]|false|Options for multi-choice or single-select attributes|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» attributeType|text|
|» attributeType|user|
|» attributeType|number|
|» attributeType|single-select|
|» attributeType|date|
|» attributeType|boolean|
|» attributeType|multi-choice|
|» objectType|companies|
|» objectType|deals|

## Update an attribute

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/attributes/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "label": "New label",
    "optionsLabels": [
      {
        "key": "value_1",
        "value": "Updated value"
      }
    ],
    "objectType": "companies"
  }'
```

`PATCH /crm/attributes/{id}`

Update an existing custom attribute''s label or options. You can rename the attribute label or modify the available options for `single-select` and `multi-choice` attribute types. System-default attributes cannot be modified except for specific editable fields.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "label": "New label",
  "optionsLabels": [
    {
      "key": "value_1",
      "value": "Updated value"
    }
  ],
  "objectType": "companies"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Attribute ID|
|body|body|object|true|Update an attribute details|
|» label|body|string|false|Attribute display label|
|» optionsLabels|body|[object]|false|Updated labels for selectable options|
|» » key|body|string|true|Internal option identifier|
|» » value|body|string|true|Display label for the option|
|» objectType|body|string|false|The type of object the attribute belongs to, it cannot be updated after creation|

#### Enumerated Values

|» objectType|deals|

## Get all deals

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/deals \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /crm/deals`

Retrieve a paginated list of deals with optional filtering, sorting, and search capabilities. Results can be filtered by attributes such as deal name or owner, linked companies, linked contacts, or modification/creation timestamps. Default sort order is descending by creation date.

<h3 id="get-all-deals-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filters[attributes.deal_name]|query|string|false|Filter by attributes. If you have a filter for the owner on your end, please send it as filters[attributes.deal_owner] and utilize the account email for the filtering.|
|filters[attributes.deal_owner]|query|string|false|Filter by the deal owner. Pass the account email address of the deal owner.|
|filters[attributes.deal_stage]|query|string|false|Filter by the deal stage. Pass the stage id, retrievable from GET /crm/pipeline/details/{pipelineID}.|
|filters[attributes.pipeline]|query|string|false|Filter by the pipeline. Pass the pipeline id, retrievable from GET /crm/pipeline/details/{pipelineID}.|
|filters[linkedCompaniesIds]|query|string|false|Filter by linked companies ids|
|filters[linkedContactsIds]|query|string|false|Filter by linked contacts ids|
|modifiedSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the deals modified after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.|
|createdSince|query|string|false|Filter (urlencoded) the deals created after a given UTC date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). Prefer to pass your timezone in date-time format for accurate result.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document of the page|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order. Default order is **descending** by creation if `sort` is not passed|
|sortBy|query|string|false|The field used to sort field names.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{

    {
      "id": "629475917295261d9b1f4403",
```

## Create a deal

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/deals \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "attributes": {
      "amount": 12,
      "deal_owner": "6093d2425a9b436e9519d034"
    },
    "linkedCompaniesIds": [
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
    ],
    "linkedContactsIds": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ],
    "name": "Deal: Connect with company"
  }'
```

`POST /crm/deals`

Create a new deal in the CRM with the specified name, attributes, and optional associations to contacts and companies. You can assign the deal to a specific pipeline and stage by providing `pipeline` and `deal_stage` attribute IDs, which can be retrieved from the pipeline details endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "amount": 12,
    "deal_owner": "6093d2425a9b436e9519d034"
  },
  "linkedCompaniesIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
  ],
  "linkedContactsIds": [
    1,
    2,
    3
  ],
  "name": "Deal: Connect with company"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-deal-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Deal create data.|
|» attributes|body|object|false|Attributes for deal creation To assign owner of a Deal you can send attributes.deal_owner and utilize the account email or ID. If you want to create a deal on a specific pipeline and stage you can use the following attributes `pipeline` and `deal_stage`. Pipeline and deal_stage are ids you can fetch using this endpoint `/crm/pipeline/details/{pipelineID}`<br>|
|» linkedCompaniesIds|body|[string(objectID)]|false|Company ids to be linked with deal|
|» linkedContactsIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Contact ids to be linked with deal|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of deal|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "61a5cd07ca1347c82306ad06"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-deal-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created new Deal|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned when invalid data posted|None|

<h3 id="create-a-deal-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Unique deal id|

## Import deals(creation and updation)

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/deals/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'mapping={}'
```

`POST /crm/deals/import`

Import deals from a CSV file with mapping options.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: false
mapping: {}
```

<h3 id="import-dealscreation-and-updation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|false|The CSV file to upload.The file should have the first row as the mapping attribute. Some default attribute names are (a) deal_id [brevo mongoID to update deals] (b) associated_contact (c) associated_company (f) any other attribute with internal name<br>|
|» mapping|body|object|false|The mapping options in JSON format. Here is an example of the JSON structure: ```json {<br>  "link_entities": true, // Determines whether to link related entities during the import process<br>  "unlink_entities": false, // Determines whether to unlink related entities during the import process<br>  "update_existing_records": true, // Determines whether to update based on deal ID or treat every row as create<br>  "unset_empty_attributes": false // Determines whether to unset a specific attribute during update if the values input is blank<br>} ```<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "processId": 50
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Bad request : With reason"
}
```

<h3 id="import-dealscreation-and-updation-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|Successfully imported deals|Inline|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string|false|none|none|

api-key, partner-key
</aside>

## Link and Unlink a deal with contacts and companies

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/deals/link-unlink/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "linkCompanyIds": [
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
    ],
    "linkContactIds": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ],
    "unlinkCompanyIds": [
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045994",
      "61a5ce58c5d479576104595",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045996"
    ],
    "unlinkContactIds": [
      4,
      5,
      6
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /crm/deals/link-unlink/{id}`

Link or unlink contacts and companies with a specific deal in a single request. You can simultaneously link new contacts/companies and unlink existing ones by providing the respective ID arrays in the request body.

> Body parameter

```json
{
```

## Update a deal

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/deals/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "attributes": {
      "amount": 12,
      "deal_owner": "6093d2425a9b436e9519d034"
    },
    "linkedCompaniesIds": [
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
    ],
    "linkedContactsIds": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ],
    "name": "Deal: Connect with client"
  }'
```

`PATCH /crm/deals/{id}`

Update an existing deal''s attributes, name, linked contacts, or linked companies. Note that passing `linkedContactsIds` or `linkedCompaniesIds` replaces the entire list of associations, so omitted IDs will be removed. To move a deal to a different pipeline or stage, provide both the `pipeline` and `deal_stage` attribute IDs.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "amount": 12,
    "deal_owner": "6093d2425a9b436e9519d034"
  },
  "linkedCompaniesIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
  ],
  "linkedContactsIds": [
    1,
    2,
    3
  ],
  "name": "Deal: Connect with client"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-deal-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|Updated deal details.|
|» attributes|body|object|false|Attributes for deal update To assign owner of a Deal you can send attributes.deal_owner and utilize the account email or ID. If you wish to update the pipeline of a deal you need to provide the `pipeline` and the `deal_stage` Pipeline and deal_stage are ids you can fetch using this endpoint `/crm/pipeline/details/{pipelineID}`<br>|
|» linkedCompaniesIds|body|[string(objectID)]|false|Warning - Using PATCH on linkedCompaniesIds replaces the list of linked companies. Omitted IDs will be removed.|
|» linkedContactsIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Warning - Using PATCH on linkedContactIds replaces the list of linked contacts. Omitted IDs will be removed.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of deal|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

|dateTo|query|integer|false|dateTo to date range filter type (timestamp in milliseconds)|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document of the page|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|

## Upload a file

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/files \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

`POST /crm/files`

Upload a file and associate it with a contact, company, or deal. The file must be sent as multipart form data with a maximum size of 10 MB. You can optionally link the file to a specific entity by providing the corresponding entity ID.

```yaml
contactId: 0
dealId: string
file: string
```

## Get all notes

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/notes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /crm/notes`

Retrieve a paginated list of CRM notes with optional filtering by entity type, entity IDs, and date range. Results are sorted by creation date in descending order by default, with a default limit of 50 notes per page.

<h3 id="get-all-notes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|entity|query|string|false|Filter by note entity type|
|entityIds|query|string|false|Filter by note entity IDs|
|dateFrom|query|integer|false|dateFrom to date range filter type (timestamp in milliseconds)|
|dateTo|query|integer|false|dateTo to date range filter type (timestamp in milliseconds)|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document of the page|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order. Default order is **descending** by creation if `sort` is not passed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|entity|companies|
|entity|deals|
|entity|contacts|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

## Create a note

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/notes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "companyIds": [
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991"
    ],
    "contactIds": [
      247,
      1,
      2
    ],
    "dealIds": [
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991"
    ],
    "text": "<p>Meeting notes: <b>Action item</b> - visit <a href=\"https://www.brevo.com/\">Brevo</a> for details.</p>"
  }'
```

`POST /crm/notes`

Create a new CRM note and optionally associate it with contacts, companies, or deals. The note text content is required, and you can link the note to multiple entities simultaneously during creation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "companyIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991"
  ],
  "contactIds": [
    247,
    1,
    2
  ],
  "dealIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991"
  ],
  "text": "<p>Meeting notes: <b>Action item</b> - visit <a href=\"https://www.brevo.com/\">Brevo</a> for details.</p>"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-note-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[NoteData](#schemanotedata)|true|Note data to create a note.|
|» companyIds|body|[string]|false|Company Ids linked to a note|
|» contactIds|body|[integer]|false|Contact Ids linked to a note|
|» dealIds|body|[string]|false|Deal Ids linked to a note|
|» text|body|string|true|Content of the note. Supports HTML for rich text formatting. Supported tags include: `<p>` (paragraph), `<b>` / `<strong>` (bold), `<i>` / `<em>` (italic), `<u>` (underline), `<br>` (line break), `<a href="...">` (labelled hyperlink). Example labelled link: `<a href="https://example.com">Link text</a>`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "61a5cd07ca1347c82306ad09"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

> 415 Response

```json
}
```

`PATCH /crm/notes/{id}`

Update an existing CRM note''s text content and its associations with contacts, companies, or deals. You can modify the note text, change the pinned status, or update the linked entities.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "companyIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991"
  ],
  "contactIds": [
    247,
    1,
    2
  ],
  "dealIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991"
  ],
  "text": "<p>Meeting notes: <b>Action item</b> - visit <a href=\"https://www.brevo.com/\">Brevo</a> for details.</p>"
}
```

|» contactIds|body|[integer]|false|Contact Ids linked to a note|
|» dealIds|body|[string]|false|Deal Ids linked to a note|
|» text|body|string|true|Content of the note. Supports HTML for rich text formatting. Supported tags include: `<p>` (paragraph), `<b>` / `<strong>` (bold), `<i>` / `<em>` (italic), `<u>` (underline), `<br>` (line break), `<a href="...">` (labelled hyperlink). Example labelled link: `<a href="https://example.com">Link text</a>`.|

## Get all tasks

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/tasks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /crm/tasks`

Retrieve a paginated list of CRM tasks with optional filtering by task type, status, date range, assignee, and linked entities (contacts, deals, companies). Results are sorted by creation date in descending order by default, with a default limit of 50 tasks per page.

<h3 id="get-all-tasks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[type]|query|string|false|Filter by task type (ID)|
|filter[status]|query|string|false|Filter by task status|
|filter[date]|query|string|false|Filter by date|
|filter[assignTo]|query|string|false|Filter by the "assignTo" ID. You can utilize account emails for the "assignTo" attribute.|
|filter[contacts]|query|string|false|Filter by contact ids|
|filter[deals]|query|string|false|Filter by deals ids|
|filter[companies]|query|string|false|Filter by companies ids|
|dateFrom|query|integer|false|dateFrom to date range filter type (timestamp in milliseconds)|
|dateTo|query|integer|false|dateTo to date range filter type (timestamp in milliseconds)|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document of the page|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents per page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order. Default order is **descending** by creation if `sort` is not passed|
|sortBy|query|string|false|The field used to sort field names.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter[status]|done|
|filter[status]|undone|
|filter[date]|overdue|
|filter[date]|today|
|filter[date]|tomorrow|
|filter[date]|week|
|filter[date]|range|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

## Create a task

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/crm/tasks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "assignToId": "5faab4b7f195bb3c4c31e62a",
    "companiesIds": [
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
    ],
    "contactsIds": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ],
    "date": "2021-11-01T17:44:54.668Z",
    "dealsIds": [
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
      "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
    ],
    "done": false,
    "duration": 600000,
    "name": "Task: Connect with client",
    "notes": "In communication with client for resolution of queries.",
    "reminder": {
      "types": [
        "email"
      ],
      "unit": "minutes",
      "value": 10
    },
    "taskTypeId": "61a5cd07ca1347c82306ad09"
  }'
```

`POST /crm/tasks`

Create a new CRM task with the specified name, type, due date, and optional associations to contacts, companies, or deals. A task requires a name, task type ID, and due date at minimum. You can also set a duration, notes, a reminder, and assign the task to a specific user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assignToId": "5faab4b7f195bb3c4c31e62a",
  "companiesIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
  ],
  "contactsIds": [
    1,
    2,
    3
  ],
  "date": "2021-11-01T17:44:54.668Z",
  "dealsIds": [
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045990",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045991",
    "61a5ce58c5d4795761045992"
  ],
  "done": false,
  "duration": 600000,
  "name": "Task: Connect with client",
  "notes": "In communication with client for resolution of queries.",
  "reminder": {
    "types": [
      "email"
    ],
    "unit": "minutes",
    "value": 10
  },
  "taskTypeId": "61a5cd07ca1347c82306ad09"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Task name.|
|» assignToId|body|string|false|To assign a task to a user you can use either the account email or ID.|
|» companiesIds|body|[string]|false|Companies ids for companies a task is linked to|
|» contactsIds|body|[integer]|false|Contact ids for contacts linked to this task|
|» date|body|string(date-time)|true|Task due date and time|
|» dealsIds|body|[string]|false|Deal ids for deals a task is linked to|
|» done|body|boolean|false|Task marked as done|
|» duration|body|integer(int64)|false|Duration of task in milliseconds [1 minute = 60000 ms]|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of task|
|» notes|body|string|false|Notes added to a task|
|» reminder|body|[TaskReminder](#schemataskreminder)|false|Task reminder date/time for a task|
|» taskTypeId|body|string|true|Id for type of task e.g Call / Email / Meeting etc.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "61a5cd07ca1347c82306ad06"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-task-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created new task|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned when invalid data posted|None|

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Send a WhatsApp message

<a id="opIdsendWhatsappMessage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/whatsapp/sendMessage \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "contactNumbers": [
      919876543210
    ],
    "params": {
      "FNAME": "Joe",
      "LNAME": "Doe"
    },
    "senderNumber": 919876543210,
    "templateId": 123
  }'
```

`POST /whatsapp/sendMessage`

<Note>You can use this API for WhatsApp only if you have setup your WhatsApp account on Brevo platform. To setup your WhatsApp account, follow the steps in the guide below.
[Activating Whatsapp](https://developers.brevo.com/docs/whatsapp-campaigns-1) in your account</Note>
This endpoint is used to send a WhatsApp message. <br/>(**The first message you send using the API must contain a Template ID. You must create a template on WhatsApp on the Brevo platform to fetch the Template ID.**)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "contactNumbers": [
    919876543210
  ],
  "params": {
    "FNAME": "Joe",
    "LNAME": "Doe"
  },
  "senderNumber": 919876543210,
  "templateId": 123
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-whatsapp-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to send WhatsApp message|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» contactNumbers|body|[string(mobile)]|true|List of phone numbers of the contacts|
|» params|body|object|false|Pass the set of attributes to customize the template. For example, {"FNAME":"Joe", "LNAME":"Doe"}.|
|» senderNumber|body|string(mobile)|true|WhatsApp Number with country code. Example, 85264318721|
|» templateId|body|integer|true|ID of the template to send|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» contactNumbers|body|[string(mobile)]|true|List of phone numbers of the contacts|
|» senderNumber|body|string(mobile)|true|WhatsApp Number with country code. Example, 85264318721|
|» text|body|string|true|Text to be sent as message body (will be overridden if templateId is passed in the same request)|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "messageId": "23befbae-1505-47a8-bd27-e30ef739f32c"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

## Get all your WhatsApp activity (unaggregated events)

<a id="opIdgetWhatsappEventReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/whatsapp/statistics/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /whatsapp/statistics/events`

This endpoint will show the unaggregated statistics for WhatsApp activity (30 days by default if `startDate` and `endDate` or `days` is not passed. The date range can not exceed 90 days)

<h3 id="get-all-your-whatsapp-activity-unaggregated-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number limitation for the result returned|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Beginning point in the list to retrieve from|
|startDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if endDate is used.** Starting date of the report (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be lower than equal to endDate<br>|
|endDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if startDate is used.** Ending date of the report (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be greater than equal to startDate<br>|
|days|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of days in the past including today (positive integer). _Not compatible with 'startDate' and 'endDate'_<br>|
|contactNumber|query|string(mobile)|false|Filter results for specific contact (WhatsApp Number with country code. Example, 85264318721)|
|event|query|string|false|Filter the report for a specific event type|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|event|sent|
|event|delivered|
|event|read|
|event|error|
|event|unsubscribe|
|event|reply|
|event|soft-bounce|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "events": [
    {
      "contactNumber": 919876543211,
      "date": "2017-03-12T12:30:00Z",
      "event": "sent",
      "messageId": "23befbae-1505-47a8-bd27-e30ef739f32c",
      "senderNumber": 919876543210
    },
    {
      "contactNumber": 919876543211,
      "date": "2017-03-12T12:30:00Z",
      "event": "error",
      "messageId": "23befbae-1505-47a8-bd27-e30ef739f32c",
      "reason": "error reason",
      "senderNumber": 919876543210
    },
    {
      "contactNumber": 919876543211,
      "date": "2017-03-12T12:30:00Z",
      "event": "soft-bounce",
      "messageId": "23befbae-1505-47a8-bd27-e30ef739f32c",
      "reason": "invalid whatsapp contact",
      "senderNumber": 919876543210
    },
    {
      "body": "body only in case of text reply & url will be empty",
      "contactNumber": 919876543211,
      "date": "2017-03-12T12:30:00Z",
      "event": "reply",
      "mediaUrl": "media url only in case media reply & body will be empty",
      "messageId": "23befbae-1505-47a8-bd27-e30ef739f32c",
      "senderNumber": 919876543210
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="brevo-api-transactional-emails">Transactional emails</h1>

## Get the list of blocked or unsubscribed transactional contacts

<a id="opIdgetTransacBlockedContacts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/blockedContacts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /smtp/blockedContacts`

Retrieve a paginated list of transactional contacts that have been blocked or unsubscribed, along with the reason for blocking (e.g. hard bounce, admin blocked, spam complaint, or unsubscription via email/API/Marketing Automation). Both `startDate` and `endDate` must be provided together when filtering by date range, and neither date can be in the future. Results default to 50 per page (max 100) and are sorted in descending order of record creation unless overridden with the `sort` parameter.

<h3 id="get-the-list-of-blocked-or-unsubscribed-transactional-contacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if endDate is used.** Starting date (YYYY-MM-DD) from which you want to fetch the blocked or unsubscribed contacts<br>|
|endDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if startDate is used.** Ending date (YYYY-MM-DD) till which you want to fetch the blocked or unsubscribed contacts<br>|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents returned per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document on the page|
|senders|query|[string]|false|Comma separated list of emails of the senders from which contacts are blocked or unsubscribed|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "contacts": [
    {
      "blockedAt": "2017-05-01T12:30:00Z",
      "email": "abc@xyz.com",
      "reason": {
        "code": "adminBlocked",
        "message": "Admin blocked"
      },
      "senderEmail": "ez312@gmal.com"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<h3 id="get-the-list-of-blocked-or-unsubscribed-transactional-contacts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|List of blocked or unsubscribed transactional contacts|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|bad request|Inline|

<h3 id="get-the-list-of-blocked-or-unsubscribed-transactional-contacts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contacts|[object]|false|none|none|
|» blockedAt|string|true|none|Date when the contact was blocked or unsubscribed on|
|» email|string(email)|true|none|Email address of the blocked or unsubscribed contact|
|» reason|object|true|none|Reason for blocking / unsubscribing|
|» » code|string|false|none|Reason code for blocking / unsubscribing (This code is safe for comparison)|
|» » message|string|false|none|Reason for blocking / unsubscribing (This string is not safe for comparison)|
|» senderEmail|string(email)|true|none|Sender email address of the blocked or unsubscribed contact|
|count|integer(int64)|false|none|Count of blocked or unsubscribed contact|

#### Enumerated Values

## Unblock or resubscribe a transactional contact

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/blockedContacts/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /smtp/blockedContacts/{email}`

Unblock or resubscribe a transactional contact by removing their email address from the blacklist. The email address must be URL-encoded in the path parameter and must be a valid email format. If the contact is not found in the blocklist, a 404 error is returned.

## Send a transactional email

<a id="opIdsendTransacEmail"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/email \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "sender": {
      "name": "Alex from Brevo",
      "email": "hello@brevo.com"
    },
    "to": [
      {
        "email": "johndoe@example.com",
        "name": "John Doe"
      }
    ],
    "subject": "Hello from Brevo!",
    "htmlContent": "<html><head></head><body><p>Hello,</p>This is my first transactional email sent from Brevo.</p></body></html>"
  }'
```

`POST /smtp/email`

Send a transactional email to one or more recipients, either using inline HTML content or a pre-built template via `templateId`. You can schedule emails for future delivery using `scheduledAt` (UTC, up to 5-minute delay), send multiple personalized versions with `messageVersions` (max 2000 total recipients, 99 per version), and attach files via URL or base64-encoded content. A `sender` and `subject` are required when no `templateId` is provided; when a `templateId` is used, the template''s sender and subject are applied unless overridden.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sender": {
    "name": "Alex from Brevo",
    "email": "hello@brevo.com"
  },
  "to": [
    {
      "email": "johndoe@example.com",
      "name": "John Doe"
    }
  ],
  "subject": "Hello from Brevo!",
  "htmlContent": "<html><head></head><body><p>Hello,</p>This is my first transactional email sent from Brevo.</p></body></html>"
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-transactional-email-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Request body parameters for sending a transactional email|
|» attachment|body|[object]|false|Array of attachment objects. Each attachment must include either an absolute URL (no local file paths) or base64-encoded content, along with the attachment filename. The `name` field is required when `content` is provided. Supported file extensions: xlsx, xls, ods, docx, docm, doc, csv, pdf, txt, gif, jpg, jpeg, png, tif, tiff, rtf, bmp, cgm, css, shtml, html, htm, zip, xml, ppt, pptx, tar, ez, ics, mobi, msg, pub, eps, odt, mp3, m4a, m4v, wma, ogg, flac, wav, aif, aifc, aiff, mp4, mov, avi, mkv, mpeg, mpg, wmv, pkpass, xlsm. When `templateId` is specified: if the template uses the New Template Language format, both `url` and `content` attachment types are supported; if the template uses the Old Template Language format, the `attachment` parameter is ignored.<br>|
|» » content|body|string(byte)|false|Base64-encoded attachment data|
|» » name|body|string|false|Attachment filename. Required when `content` is provided.<br>|
|» » url|body|string(url)|false|Absolute URL of the attachment. Local file paths are not supported.<br>|
|» batchId|body|string|false|UUIDv4 identifier for the scheduled batch of transactional emails. If omitted, a valid UUIDv4 batch identifier is automatically generated.|
|» bcc|body|[object]|false|Array of BCC recipient objects. Each object contains an email address and an optional name.<br>|
|» » contactPixelTrackingConsent|body|boolean|false|Consent of the recipient in bcc for open (pixel) and click tracking, resolved by the sender at send time. Considered only if the per-contact pixel tracking consent feature is enabled for your account. Pass `true` if this recipient has consented to open and click tracking, in which case the open pixel and tracked links identify the recipient. Pass `false` to anonymise the open and click events (counted in aggregate statistics only). If it is not passed, the recipient is treated as unknown consent status and the email is still sent (the open and click are anonymised unless your account tracks unknown-consent contacts). A value other than `true`/`false` is rejected. Ignored when the feature is not enabled for your account.<br>|
|» » email|body|string(email)|true|BCC recipient email address|
|» » name|body|string|false|Display name of the BCC recipient. Maximum length is 70 characters.<br>|
|» » removeTrackingPixel|body|boolean|false|Pass `true` to send the recipient in bcc no open pixel, so no open is recorded for them, not even in aggregate statistics. Only available to Enterprise plans: for other accounts the field is accepted but ignored. Considered only if the recipient is not tracked: `contactPixelTrackingConsent` is `false`, or not passed and your account does not track unknown-consent contacts. Click tracking is unchanged. If `false` or not passed, the open pixel is added as usual. A value other than `true`/`false` is rejected.<br>|
|» cc|body|[object]|false|Array of CC recipient objects. Each object contains an email address and an optional name.<br>|
|» » contactPixelTrackingConsent|body|boolean|false|Consent of the recipient in cc for open (pixel) and click tracking, resolved by the sender at send time. Considered only if the per-contact pixel tracking consent feature is enabled for your account. Pass `true` if this recipient has consented to open and click tracking, in which case the open pixel and tracked links identify the recipient. Pass `false` to anonymise the open and click events (counted in aggregate statistics only). If it is not passed, the recipient is treated as unknown consent status and the email is still sent (the open and click are anonymised unless your account tracks unknown-consent contacts). A value other than `true`/`false` is rejected. Ignored when the feature is not enabled for your account.<br>|

If `false` or not passed, the open pixel is added as usual. A value other than `true`/`false` is rejected.<br>|

|» » removeTrackingPixel|body|boolean|false|Pass `true` to send the recipient no open pixel, so no open is recorded for them, not even in aggregate statistics. Only available to Enterprise plans: for other accounts the field is accepted but ignored. Considered only if the recipient is not tracked: `contactPixelTrackingConsent` is `false`, or not passed and your account does not track unknown-consent contacts. Click tracking is unchanged. If `false` or not passed, the open pixel is added as usual. A value other than `true`/`false` is rejected.<br>|

```json
  "messageId": "<201798300811.5787683@relay.domain.com>"
}
```

```json
}
```

## Fetch scheduled emails by batchId or messageId

<a id="opIdgetScheduledEmailById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/emailStatus/4320f270-a4e3-4a2e-b591-edfe30a5e627 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /smtp/emailStatus/{identifier}`

Fetch scheduled batch of emails by batchId or single scheduled email by messageId (Can retrieve data upto 30 days old)

<h3 id="fetch-scheduled-emails-by-batchid-or-messageid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|identifier|path|string|true|The `batchId` of scheduled emails batch (must be a valid UUIDv4) or the `messageId` of scheduled email (enclosed in angle brackets with @ sign, e.g. `<...@domain>`). When using `messageId`, the `limit`, `offset`, `sort`, and `status` query parameters are ignored.|
|startDate|query|string(date)|false|Mandatory if `endDate` is used. Starting date (YYYY-MM-DD) from which you want to fetch the list. Cannot be more than 30 days older than the current date.|
|endDate|query|string(date)|false|Mandatory if `startDate` is used. Ending date (YYYY-MM-DD) till which you want to fetch the list. Maximum time period that can be selected is one month.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed. Not valid when identifier is `messageId`.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter the records by `status` of the scheduled email batch or message. Not valid when identifier is `messageId`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents returned per page. Not valid when identifier is `messageId`.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document on the page.  Not valid when identifier is `messageId`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|
|status|processed|
|status|inProgress|
|status|queued|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "batches": [
    {
      "createdAt": "2022-02-26T11:36:43.576000000Z",
      "scheduledAt": "2022-02-28T11:36:43.576000000Z",
      "status": "queued"
    },
    {
      "createdAt": "2022-02-24T11:36:43.576000000Z",
      "scheduledAt": "2022-02-25T11:36:43.576000000Z",
      "status": "processed"
    },
    {
      "createdAt": "2022-02-25T11:36:43.576000000Z",
      "scheduledAt": "2022-02-26T11:36:43.576000000Z",
      "status": "inProgress"
    }
  ],
  "count": 3
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

## Get the list of transactional emails on the basis of allowed filters

<a id="opIdgetTransacEmailsList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/emails \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /smtp/emails`

This endpoint will show the list of emails for past 30 days by default. To retrieve emails before that time, please pass startDate and endDate in query filters.

<h3 id="get-the-list-of-transactional-emails-on-the-basis-of-allowed-filters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email|query|string|false|**Mandatory if templateId and messageId are not passed in query filters.** Email address to which transactional email has been sent.<br>|
|templateId|query|integer(int64)|false|**Mandatory if email and messageId are not passed in query filters.** Id of the template that was used to compose transactional email.<br>|
|messageId|query|string|false|**Mandatory if templateId and email are not passed in query filters.** Message ID of the transactional email sent.<br>|
|startDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if endDate is used.** Starting date (YYYY-MM-DD) from which you want to fetch the list. **Maximum time period that can be selected is one month**.<br>|
|endDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if startDate is used.** Ending date (YYYY-MM-DD) till which you want to fetch the list. **Maximum time period that can be selected is one month.**<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents returned per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document in the page|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 120,
  "transactionalEmails": [
    {
      "date": "2019-05-25T11:53:26Z",
      "email": "abc@xyz.com",
      "messageId": "<201798300811.5787683@relay.domain.com>",
      "subject": "summer camp",
      "templateId": 15,
      "uuid": "5a78c-209ok98262910-std2341"
    },
    {
      "date": "2019-05-25T07:28:11Z",
      "email": "test@test.com",
      "messageId": "<201798300811.5700093@relay.domain.com>",
      "subject": "details verification",
      "templateId": 15,
      "uuid": "5a78c-209ok98262910-s99a341"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<Note title="How to get uuid">You can get the uuid using either of the following methods:

## Delete an SMTP transactional log

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/log/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /smtp/log/{identifier}`

Delete SMTP transactional log entries identified by a message ID (enclosed in angle brackets with an @ sign) or a valid email address. Optionally narrow the deletion to a specific date range using `from_date` and `to_date` query parameters (YYYY-MM-DD format). The operation also removes any associated stored email preview content.

<h3 id="delete-an-smtp-transactional-log-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|identifier|path|string|true|MessageId or email address of the transactional log(s) to delete. Must be a valid message ID (enclosed in angle brackets with @ sign) or a valid email address.|
|from_date|query|string|false|Starting date (YYYY-MM-DD) to narrow down logs for deletion|
|to_date|query|string|false|Ending date (YYYY-MM-DD) to narrow down logs for deletion|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
```

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/statistics/events \

```

`GET /smtp/statistics/events`

This endpoint will show the aggregated stats for past 30 days by default if `startDate` and `endDate` OR `days` is not passed. The date range can not exceed 90 days

<h3 id="get-all-your-transactional-email-activity-unaggregated-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number limitation for the result returned|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Beginning point in the list to retrieve from.|
|startDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if endDate is used.** Starting date of the report (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be lower than equal to endDate<br>|
|endDate|query|string|false|**Mandatory if startDate is used.** Ending date of the report (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be greater than equal to startDate<br>|
|days|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of days in the past including today (positive integer, maximum 90). _Not compatible with 'startDate' and 'endDate'_. Defaults to 30 if neither dates nor days are provided.<br>|
|email|query|string(email)|false|Filter the report for a specific email addresses|
|event|query|string|false|Filter the report for a specific event type|
|tags|query|string|false|Filter the report for tags (serialized and urlencoded array)|
|messageId|query|string|false|Filter on a specific message id|
|templateId|query|integer(int64)|false|Filter on a specific template id|

## Generate the rendered preview of transactional template

<a id="opIdpostPreviewSmtpEmailTemplates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/template/preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "john.doe@example.com",
    "params": {
      "Firstname": "John",
      "Lastname": "Doe"
    },
    "templateId": 22
  }'
```

`POST /smtp/template/preview`

Generate a fully rendered preview of a transactional email template by resolving dynamic variables. Provide either an `email` address (to populate variables from the contact''s attributes) or a `params` object with key-value pairs for manual substitution; at least one of these is required alongside the mandatory `templateId`. The response includes the rendered HTML, subject, sender details, preview text, and any feed names used in the template.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "john.doe@example.com",
  "params": {
    "Firstname": "John",
    "Lastname": "Doe"
  },
  "templateId": 22
}
```

<h3 id="generate-the-rendered-preview-of-transactional-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Values to fetch Template preview|
|» email|body|string|false|Email of the contact.(Required if params not provided)|
|» params|body|object|false|Key-value pairs of dynamic parameters for template rendering.(Required if email not provided) For example: **{"Firstname":"John", "Lastname":"Doe"}**<br>|
|» » Firstname|body|string|false|firstname of the contact. **Dynamic parameter**<br>|
|» » Lastname|body|string|false|Lastname of the contact. **Dynamic parameter**|
|» templateId|body|integer|true|Id of the template.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "fromEmail": "nikon.doe@example.com",
  "fromName": "Nikon Doe",
  "html": "<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><title>Preview html content</title></head><body><p>html content</p></body></html>",
  "previewText": "Preview text",
  "subject": "Template preview subject",
  "usedFeedNames": "[\"feed_1\",\"feed_2\"]"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-the-rendered-preview-of-transactional-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|successfully fetched template's preview fields|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|bad request|Inline|

<h3 id="generate-the-rendered-preview-of-transactional-template-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fromEmail|string|false|none|Sender email address|
|fromName|string|false|none|Sender Name|
|html|string|false|none|Html content of the template|
|previewText|string|false|none|Preview text of the template|
|subject|string|false|none|subject of the template|
|usedFeedNames|[string]|false|none|none|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|true|none|Error code displayed in case of a failure|
|message|string|true|none|Readable message associated to the failure|

#### Enumerated Values

## Get the list of email templates

<a id="opIdgetSmtpTemplates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/templates \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /smtp/templates`

Retrieve a paginated list of all transactional email templates (including automation templates) with their details such as name, subject, sender, status, HTML content, and timestamps. Results default to 50 per page (max 1000) and are sorted in descending creation order unless overridden. You can filter by active/inactive status using `templateStatus` and by editor type using `editorType` (currently only `richTextEditor` is supported).

<h3 id="get-the-list-of-email-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|templateStatus|query|boolean|false|Filter on the status of the template. Active = true, inactive = false|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of documents returned per page|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Index of the first document in the page|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed|
|editorType|query|string|false|Filter on the editor type used to create the template. Currently only `richTextEditor` is supported as a filter value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|
|editorType|richTextEditor|

## Create an email template

<a id="opIdcreateSmtpTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/templates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "attachmentUrl": "https://attachment.domain.com",
    "htmlContent": "The order n°xxxxx has been confirmed. Thanks for your purchase",
    "htmlUrl": "https://html.domain.com",
    "isActive": true,
    "replyTo": "support@myshop.com",
    "sender": {
      "email": "contact@myshop.com",
      "id": 3,
      "name": "Mary from MyShop"
    },
    "subject": "Thanks for your purchase !",
    "tag": "OrderConfirmation",
    "templateName": "Order Confirmation - EN",
    "toField": "{FNAME} {LNAME}"
  }'
```

`POST /smtp/templates`

Create a new transactional email template with the specified sender, subject, and content. The `sender`, `subject`, and `templateName` fields are required. Template content can be provided via `htmlContent` (minimum 10 characters) or `htmlUrl`; at least one must be supplied. Templates are created as inactive by default unless `isActive` is explicitly set to `true`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attachmentUrl": "https://attachment.domain.com",
  "htmlContent": "The order n°xxxxx has been confirmed. Thanks for your purchase",
  "htmlUrl": "https://html.domain.com",
  "isActive": true,
  "replyTo": "support@myshop.com",
  "sender": {
    "email": "contact@myshop.com",
    "id": 3,
    "name": "Mary from MyShop"
  },
  "subject": "Thanks for your purchase !",
  "tag": "OrderConfirmation",
  "templateName": "Order Confirmation - EN",
  "toField": "{FNAME} {LNAME}"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-email-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|values to update in transactional email template|
|» attachmentUrl|body|string(url)|false|Absolute url of the attachment (**no local file**). Extension allowed: #### xlsx, xls, ods, docx, docm, doc, csv, pdf, txt, gif, jpg, jpeg, png, tif, tiff, rtf, bmp, cgm, css, shtml, html, htm, zip, xml, ppt, pptx, tar, ez, ics, mobi, msg, pub and eps'<br>|
|» htmlContent|body|string|false|Body of the message (HTML version). The field must have more than 10 characters. **REQUIRED if htmlUrl is empty**<br>|
|» htmlUrl|body|string(url)|false|Url which contents the body of the email message. REQUIRED if htmlContent is empty|
|» isActive|body|boolean|false|Status of template. isActive = true means template is active and isActive = false means template is inactive|
|» replyTo|body|string(email)|false|Email on which campaign recipients will be able to reply to|
|» sender|body|object|true|Sender details including id or email and name (_optional_). Only one of either Sender's email or Sender's ID shall be passed in one request at a time. For example: **{"name":"xyz", "email":"example@abc.com"}** **{"name":"xyz", "id":123}**<br>|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|Email of the sender|
|» » id|body|integer(int64)|false|Select the sender for the template on the basis of sender id. _In order to select a sender with specific pool of IP’s, dedicated ip users shall pass id (instead of email)_.<br>|
|» » name|body|string|false|Name of the sender. **If not passed, will be set to default**<br>|
|» subject|body|string|true|Subject of the template|
|» tag|body|string|false|Tag of the template|
|» templateName|body|string|true|Name of the template|
|» toField|body|string|false|To personalize the **To** Field. If you want to include the first name and last name of your recipient, add **{FNAME} {LNAME}**. These contact attributes must already exist in your Brevo account. If input parameter **params** used please use **{{contact.FNAME}} {{contact.LNAME}}** for personalization<br>|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "id": 5
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
  "code": "method_not_allowed",
  "message": "POST Method is not allowed on this path"
}
```

## Returns the template information

<a id="opIdgetSmtpTemplate"></a>

`GET /smtp/templates/{templateId}`

Retrieve the full details of a specific transactional email template by its numeric ID or custom template identifier string. The response includes the template name, subject, sender information, HTML content, active status, creation and modification timestamps, reply-to address, tag, and a `doiTemplate` flag indicating whether the template is a double opt-in template (detected by the presence of optin-related tags or variables in the content).

|templateId|path|integer(int64) \| string|true|ID of the template. Can be a numeric template ID or a custom template identifier string (alphanumeric, hyphens, and underscores only, max 64 characters, must start with a letter).|

## Update an email template

<a id="opIdupdateSmtpTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/templates/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "attachmentUrl": "https://attachment.domain.com",
    "htmlContent": "The order n°xxxxx has been confirmed. Thanks for your purchase",
    "htmlUrl": "https://html.domain.com",
    "isActive": true,
    "replyTo": "support@myshop.com",
    "sender": {
      "email": "contact@myshop.com",
      "id": 3,
      "name": "Mary from MyShop"
    },
    "subject": "Thanks for your purchase !",
    "tag": "OrderConfirmation",
    "templateName": "Order Confirmation - EN",
    "toField": "{FNAME} {LNAME}"
  }'
```

`PUT /smtp/templates/{templateId}`

Update an existing transactional email template by its numeric ID or custom template identifier string. All fields in the request body are optional; only the provided fields will be updated. You can update the template name, subject, sender, reply-to address, HTML content (via `htmlContent` or `htmlUrl`), active status, tag, attachment URL, and the personalized `toField`. Only one of sender email or sender ID should be provided per request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attachmentUrl": "https://attachment.domain.com",
  "htmlContent": "The order n°xxxxx has been confirmed. Thanks for your purchase",
  "htmlUrl": "https://html.domain.com",
  "isActive": true,
  "replyTo": "support@myshop.com",
  "sender": {
    "email": "contact@myshop.com",
    "id": 3,
    "name": "Mary from MyShop"
  },
  "subject": "Thanks for your purchase !",
  "tag": "OrderConfirmation",
  "templateName": "Order Confirmation - EN",
  "toField": "{FNAME} {LNAME}"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-email-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|templateId|path|integer(int64) \| string|true|ID of the template. Can be a numeric template ID or a custom template identifier string.|
|body|body|object|true|values to update in transactional email template|
|» attachmentUrl|body|string(url)|false|Absolute url of the attachment (**no local file**). Extensions allowed: #### xlsx, xls, ods, docx, docm, doc, csv, pdf, txt, gif, jpg, jpeg, png, tif, tiff, rtf, bmp, cgm, css, shtml, html, htm, zip, xml, ppt, pptx, tar, ez, ics, mobi, msg, pub and eps<br>|
|» htmlContent|body|string|false|**Required if htmlUrl is empty**. If the template is designed using Drag & Drop editor via HTML content, then the design page will not have Drag & Drop editor access for that template. Body of the message (HTML must have more than 10 characters)<br>|
|» htmlUrl|body|string(url)|false|**Required if htmlContent is empty**. URL to the body of the email (HTML)<br>|
|» isActive|body|boolean|false|Status of the template. isActive = false means template is inactive, isActive = true means template is active|
|» replyTo|body|string(email)|false|Email on which campaign recipients will be able to reply to|
|» sender|body|object|false|Sender details including id or email and name (_optional_). Only one of either Sender's email or Sender's ID shall be passed in one request at a time. For example: **{"name":"xyz", "email":"example@abc.com"}** **{"name":"xyz", "id":123}**<br>|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|Email of the sender|
|» » id|body|integer(int64)|false|Select the sender for the template on the basis of sender id. _In order to select a sender with specific pool of IP’s, dedicated ip users shall pass id (instead of email)_.<br>|
|» » name|body|string|false|Name of the sender|
|» subject|body|string|false|Subject of the email|
|» tag|body|string|false|Tag of the template|
|» templateName|body|string|false|Name of the template|
|» toField|body|string|false|To personalize the **To** Field. If you want to include the first name and last name of your recipient, add **{FNAME} {LNAME}**. These contact attributes must already exist in your Brevo account. If input parameter **params** used please use **{{contact.FNAME}} {{contact.LNAME}}** for personalization<br>|

```json
}
```

## Delete an inactive email template

<a id="opIddeleteSmtpTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/templates/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /smtp/templates/{templateId}`

Permanently delete a transactional email template by its numeric ID. Only inactive templates can be deleted; attempting to delete an active template returns a 405 error. To deactivate a template before deletion, use `PUT /smtp/templates/{templateId}` with `isActive` set to `false`. Deletion also removes associated newsletter template data and triggers asynchronous cleanup of shared assets.

<h3 id="delete-an-inactive-email-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|templateId|path|integer(int64)|true|id of the template|

## Send a template to your test list

<a id="opIdsendTestTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/templates/0/sendTest \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "api-key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "emailTo": [
      "helen.jurger@example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /smtp/templates/{templateId}/sendTest`

Send a test email of the specified transactional template to one or more recipients. Provide an array of email addresses in the `emailTo` field; if left empty, the test mail is sent to your entire test list. You can send a maximum of 50 test emails per day, and all provided email addresses must be valid.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "emailTo": [
    "helen.jurger@example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-template-to-your-test-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|templateId|path|integer(int64)|true|Id of the template|
|body|body|[sendTestEmail](#schemasendtestemail)|true|none|
|» emailTo|body|[string(email)]|false|List of the email addresses of the recipients whom you wish to send the test mail. _If left empty, the test mail will be sent to your entire test list. You can not send more than 50 test emails per day_.<br>|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "blackListedEmails": [
    "jeff.dean@example.com, jim.sue@example.com"
  ],
  "code": "invalid_parameter",

  "unexistingEmails": [
    "matthew.dow@example.com, elisa.carrely@example.com"
  ],
  "withoutListEmails": [

  ]
}
```

```json
  "code": "method_not_allowed",

}
```
